articles.title: Tom Brady's 16-year-old son Benjamin appears uninterested in following his father's football legacy as music takes centre stage
articles.summary: Growing up as Tom Brady's son comes with an obvious connection to football, but Benjamin Brady is finding his own rhythm outside the sport.
articles.body: Growing up as Tom Brady's son comes with an obvious connection to football, but Benjamin Brady is finding his own rhythm outside the sport. The 16-year-old has developed a strong interest in music and DJing, giving him a creative outlet that stands apart from his father's legendary NFL career. Rather than pushing him towards the game that made him famous, Brady is making an effort to understand and support the interests that excite his son.Tom Brady opens up about Benjamin's love for music and DJingTom Brady recently offered a glimpse into his relationship with Benjamin during an appearance on Jake Humphrey's High Performance podcast on November 23. The retired quarterback spoke about how his approach to parenting has changed as his children grow older and develop interests of their own.Benjamin's passion for music has caught his attention. Brady explained that he wants to be involved in that part of his son's life, even if it takes him away from the familiar world of football."My son Benny, who's 16, he loves music and he loves deejaying. You know, I want to sit there and listen to what he's doing."The admission offered a different picture of the seven-time Super Bowl champion. For years, Brady built his reputation around discipline, preparation and an intense desire to win. Yet, at home, he is learning that supporting his children sometimes means stepping into worlds he knows very little about.He also understands that his own interests should not become expectations for his children. Instead of asking Benjamin to spend time watching football footage, Brady wants to give him the attention he needs while pursuing music.Benjamin Brady builds his own identity beyond his father's NFL legacyMusic is not an entirely new interest for Benjamin. He has previously shown an aptitude for playing the piano and learning songs by ear. His growing enthusiasm for DJing adds another dimension to his creative side.Being the son of one of the most celebrated quarterbacks in NFL history could easily bring expectations. However, Benjamin appears to be exploring interests that allow him to express himself without constantly being compared with his father.Brady also shares two other children, Jack, 19, and Vivian, 13. Each has their own interests, and the former quarterback has spoken about the importance of understanding what matters to them.For Brady, fatherhood now involves more listening and less coaching. His latest comments suggest that he wants Benjamin to enjoy discovering his own abilities rather than feel pressured to follow a familiar path.Football may always remain a major part of the Brady family story. But Benjamin's growing interest in music shows that the next generation is free to create a story of its own.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes' $325 million KC Current stepped up for struggling families with 400 gallons of milk and fresh produce
articles.summary: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes have built a strong presence in Kansas City beyond the football field.
articles.body: Patrick and Brittany Mahomes have built a strong presence in Kansas City beyond the football field. While Patrick continues to make headlines with the Chiefs, the couple also has a stake in the city's women's soccer club, the Kansas City Current. Their involvement connects them to an organisation that has been working to make a difference beyond match days. One of its notable community efforts came in September 2024, when the club helped bring essential food supplies to hundreds of local residents.Patrick and Brittany Mahomes' KC Current ownership extends beyond soccerBrittany Mahomes was part of the ownership group that launched the Kansas City Current in 2020. Patrick joined the group in January 2023, becoming the first active NFL player to hold equity in a National Women's Soccer League team.The move gave the Mahomes family another connection to Kansas City's sporting community. Brittany, a former professional soccer player, has long supported the growth of women's football. Patrick's arrival added another high-profile name to the ownership group, which also includes Chris and Angie Long.But the club's work is not limited to building a successful team. Its community partnerships have created opportunities to support families facing everyday challenges, including food insecurity.KC Current's food donation drive helps nearly 400 peopleThat commitment took a practical form on September 23, 2024, when the KC Current joined Dairy Farmers of America, Harvesters and United Way of Greater Kansas City for a food distribution event at CPKC Stadium.Dairy Farmers of America donated 400 gallons of milk, while Harvesters supplied fresh produce. The drive helped nearly 400 adults and children in the area. Volunteers also prepared more than 200 bags of produce for distribution.The event brought the club's community mission directly to local families. Instead of a traditional donation announcement, the stadium became a collection and distribution point, with residents able to receive supplies through a drive-through arrangement.KC Current players Temwa Chawinga, Hailie Mace and Jereko also took part, helping load vehicles with milk and produce. United Way helped identify households that could benefit from the support, while its partnership with the club helped bring the participating organisations together.The initiative also reflected the value of the club's relationship with Dairy Farmers of America, which had partnered with the Current in 2024. The organisations later renewed their partnership in March 2025, with plans to continue dairy donation drives and events for families experiencing food insecurity.For the Mahomes family, the Current represents more than another sporting investment. The club's community efforts show how a professional sports organisation can use its reach, partnerships and platform to support the city it calls home.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Travis Kelce's $5.35 million Ohio mansion carries a $120,000 tax bill, with $72,000 potentially benefiting local schools
articles.summary: Travis Kelce's return to Ohio has brought more than a multimillion-dollar mansion into the spotlight.
articles.body: Travis Kelce's return to Ohio has brought more than a multimillion-dollar mansion into the spotlight. His $5.35 million estate in Bratenahl could also have a financial impact on the community surrounding it. While the Kansas City Chiefs star's sprawling property reflects the success he has built through his NFL career, its estimated annual property tax bill carries an unexpected connection to public education. A significant portion of that money could support Cleveland's public schools, giving the luxury purchase a community angle beyond its impressive price tag.Travis Kelce's Ohio mansion could generate $120,000 in annual property taxesOwning a historic estate comes with responsibilities that extend well beyond its purchase price. For Kelce, those costs could include an estimated $120,000 in property taxes every year, according to an Axios report published in September 2026.The figure offers another perspective on the financial commitment behind the NFL star's Ohio residence. According to Axios Cleveland, the mansion, which reportedly spans approximately 21,000 square feet, is among the most striking residential properties in the Cleveland area. However, its size and value also mean that it could make a substantial contribution to local tax revenues.What makes the estimate particularly interesting is how that money could be distributed. Around 60% of the annual property tax bill, or approximately $72,000, could go towards the Cleveland Metropolitan School District.That is a notable amount for a single residential property to potentially contribute towards public services. It also highlights how high-value real estate can play a role in supporting communities through local taxation.Travis Kelce's mansion could bring an unexpected boost to Cleveland schoolsThe potential school funding connection adds another dimension to Kelce's investment in his home state. Cleveland Metropolitan School District serves students across the area, and property taxes form an important part of the funding structure supporting public education.Although Kelce's mansion is located in Bratenahl, the village falls within the Cleveland school district. This creates an interesting link between the property and the educational system serving the wider community.The estimated $72,000 allocation is not a personal donation from Kelce or a charitable contribution announced by the football star. Rather, it represents a potential public funding contribution through property taxation.For Kelce, whose career has brought him considerable financial success, the Ohio estate represents a connection to the place where his story began. Its possible contribution to local schools offers a reminder that expensive property purchases can have effects beyond their owners.The final tax amount and distribution would depend on the applicable property assessment and tax records. articles.title: Terry Bradshaw Says Aaron Rodgers Didn't Show 'Class' by Calling Out Mike McCarthy, Steelers
articles.summary: NFL legend Terry Bradshaw joined the chorus of voices criticizing Aaron Rodgers for his public rebuke of Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike McCarthy.
articles.body:
NFL legend Terry Bradshaw joined the chorus of voices criticizing Aaron Rodgers for his public rebuke of Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike McCarthy.

During the Fox pregame show ahead of the Dallas Cowboys and Philadelphia Eagles' Thanksgiving Day contest, Bradshaw said players should "show class on the way out" and "don't turn" on teammates, coaches and front-office executives:

Fox Sports colleague Michael Strahan was even more passionate about Rodgers, calling the four-time MVP a "rich jerk" and saying "there always seems to be smoke around Rodgers."

By now, NFL fans are well aware of the most explosive allegations Rodgers made about McCarthy during his appearance on The Pat McAfee Show .

McCarthy confirmed he said "1-2-3 Packers" in the locker room to cap off his halftime speech during the 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. An ESPN report also suggested Rodgers' general portrayal of the coach was accurate.

Even if Rodgers was telling the truth, the comments from Brady, Strahan and others make it clear the surefire Hall of Famer crossed a line.

articles.title: Jerry Jones Backs Brian Schottenheimer After Cowboys' Historic 21-Point Collapse in Loss to Eagles
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones threw his support behind coach Brian Schottenheimer after Thursday's stunning 39-38 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones threw his support behind coach Brian Schottenheimer after Thursday's stunning 39-38 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.

Jones described the result as a "bitter disappointment" and "damning setback":

He proceeded to say he has no plans to shake up the coaching staff before Dallas is back in action on Dec. 7 against the Seattle Seahawks:

The Cowboys could be headed to a third straight losing season, and Thursday feels like rock bottom.

The Eagles have basically packed it in. They traded away some proven starters. Franchise quarterback Jalen Hurts is sidelined indefinitely. Coach Nick Sirianni and his staff are once again coming under fire .

This should've been a straightforward win for Dallas, and everyone assumed that's what was in store after the Cowboys jumped ahead 21-3 in the first half and led by 21 points in the third quarter.

Instead, their porous defense was their undoing. Their secondary was carved up by Joe Milton III, whose 331 passing yards on Thanksgiving were equal to nearly half of his career output entering the day (734 yards).

When Dak Prescott got sacked on a 4th-and-1 inside the final minute, a game-winning field goal for the Eagles was inevitable.

There aren't many levers for the Cowboys to pull at this point to turn things around. The trade deadline has passed. They removed play-calling duties from defensive coordinator Christian Parker. Jones seemingly took a coaching change off the table.

Plenty of fans will believe it doesn't matter who's coaching the team when so many problems within the organization start at the top. Whether Schottenheimer stays or goes is irrelevant since Jones isn't going to fire himself.

articles.title: Cowboys' Jerry Jones Defends Mike McCarthy After Aaron Rodgers' Viral Comments on Steelers HC
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones came to the defense of Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy after Aaron Rodgers publicly put him on blast this week.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones came to the defense of Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy after Aaron Rodgers publicly put him on blast this week.

"I offered him to stay at least another year when he left. I thought he was outstanding as the head coach," Jones told reporters. "Had a great command of quarterback, offense. Can't say enough good things about him. He's frankly one of the finest people around football that I've been around. I never had the type of thing that's being said about him—I never had that in any type of consideration in my time with him extending his contract, any of that. That was never on the table. And we never had an issue within the organization."

Rodgers went no-holds-barred while criticizing McCarthy during an appearance on The Pat McAfee Show , saying the head coach sleeps through meetings or is late to them, is slow to watch film, never fostered a relationship with the defensive players and led a "1-2-3, Packers!" chant during halftime of a game this season.

He also said that some of those issues dated back to McCarthy's time leading the Green Bay Packers and Cowboys.

"It's the same thing that went on in Green Bay for a decade because the coaches and the support staff there know exactly what happened," he told McAfee, adding that he "looked into what was going on in Dallas and what happened there."

There has been plenty of pushback against Rodgers after his commentary, however:

And Jones, at least, was quick to stick up for McCarthy and defend his professionalism on Thursday.

articles.title: Jerry Jones still confident about Cowboys HC Brian Schottenheimer, doesn't expect coaching change after Thanksgiving loss to Eagles
articles.summary: The Cowboys owner has fired a head coach during the season only once in his tenure.
articles.body:
Thanksgiving wound up being a very bad night for Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer, but it apparently won't cost him his job.

Immediately after the Cowboys' collapse against the Philadelphia Eagles on Thursday , team owner Jerry Jones told reporters he doesn't expect to make a coaching change any time soon. Instead, Jones suggested continuity would give Dallas its best chance in the coming weeks.

"I wouldn't anticipate that, no, at this juncture. We can give ourselves a better chance to win these coming games and be competitive, in my mind, without coaching changes."

The Cowboys face the Seattle Seahawks in Week 13, then have a bye before facing the Los Angeles Rams on Dec. 20.

Jones went on to say he was still " confident " about Schottenheimer, but made clear that confidence was based on nothing the team showed Thursday :

"Nothing we've seen out here tonight, but you've got to look at everything. That's certainly not the thought on my mind at this particular time. We've got several more games to go and we've got to have our mind on that."

Thanksgiving really was that bad for the Cowboys, who led 28-10 at halftime and held a lead as large as 21 points near the end of the third quarter.

The team was then hit with a cascading series of disasters. Former Cowboys backup Joe Milton led the Eagles to touchdowns on three of their next four drives, with the Eagles also returning a blocked punt for a touchdown. The Cowboys still had the advantage in the final minute, but decided to go for it on fourth down in Eagles territory and watched Dak Prescott get sacked.

Eagles kicker Jake Elliott proceeded to make a 59-yard field goal in the final seconds. A Prescott interception ended the game.

Both the overall collapse and late-game decision-making left nearly every finger in Dallas pointing at Schottenheimer, who has been facing the hot seat for some time. He said he wasn't worried about such speculation after the game, via Jon Machota of The Athletic :

"I don't worry about that. I worry about the guys in that locker room. That doesn't affect me."

Schottenheimer's hire was controversial when it was first announced, as he was hardly a popular offensive coordinator under previous head coach Mike McCarthy (who is dealing with issues of his own right now) . Jones' decision to promote Schottenheimer demanded trust in his own team's operations, and the results have been a 12-16-1 record.

In more than three decades of owning the Cowboys, Jones has fired only a single head coach during the season: Wade Phillips in 2010. Jones has said he regrets that decision and that could very well be informing his thinking here, though that will hardly protect Schottenheimer in a month and a half.

articles.title: “Not an onus on defending yourself..": Jason Kelce unleashes on NFL crackback block rule as Travis Kelce questions protection for players running without the ball
articles.summary: Travis and Jason Kelce have a problem with the NFL's restrictions on crackback blocks, and neither brother held back while discussing the rule on their
articles.body: Travis and Jason Kelce have a problem with the NFL's restrictions on crackback blocks, and neither brother held back while discussing the rule on their podcast. During an episode of New Heights, the former Philadelphia Eagles center and Kansas City Chiefs tight end questioned why the league limits contact against players who are running without the football.The brothers believe players should take greater responsibility for protecting themselves on the field. Their criticism puts the NFL's player safety rules under the spotlight again, with Jason delivering a particularly blunt verdict on the restrictions. Travis Kelce questions why players get extra protection on the fieldTravis Kelce believes players should remain alert when they move around the field, particularly during kickoff situations. The Chiefs tight end made his position clear on New Heights, arguing that players should prepare for contact rather than rely on restrictions that prevent certain blocks."You're running scot-free on the kickoff. You've got to have your antennas up. This is why crackbacks should be legal, because guys just have to be on their P's and Q's.Keep your head on a swivel, man. You're on the field," Travis Kelce said on the New Heights podcast.His argument focuses on awareness and the physical demands of football. However, crackback blocks are not entirely banned under NFL rules. The league restricts specific forms of contact based on the blocker's position, movement and the type of contact involved. The regulations aim to limit dangerous hits, particularly those involving contact against players in vulnerable positions.That distinction is at the heart of the brothers' disagreement with the rule. They want players to have greater freedom to make contact, even when defenders do not carry the football. Jason Kelce calls NFL crackback block restrictions the 'dumbest rule change'Jason Kelce took the argument further on New Heights. The retired Eagles center questioned why players running without the football should receive additional protection when they are not attempting to catch a pass or carrying the ball."The idea that you're defenseless when you're running on the field is insane to me, the ball carrier isn't right there. You're not extending for a catch, you're not throwing a ball, you're just running, why is there not an onus on defending yourself?" Jason said on the New Heights podcast.Jason has spent years playing in the trenches, where blocking decisions often come down to split-second reactions. His experience as a former offensive lineman also gives him a different perspective on the restrictions, particularly when they limit what players can do to help their teammates.He did not stop at questioning the reasoning behind the rule. Jason also made his frustration clear with a blunt assessment of the NFL's decision."It's the dumbest rule change of all time, I hate it," Jason said on New Heights.The NFL continues to adjust its rules to address player safety, including concerns about head injuries and dangerous collisions. Crackback restrictions form part of those efforts, although the Kelce brothers believe the league has gone too far in limiting certain physical plays.Their criticism adds to the ongoing debate over how the NFL balances physicality with player protection. articles.title: NFL Playoff Picture 2026-27, Standings, Bracket Scenarios After Thanksgiving
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills and Chicago Bears picked up vital wins in their respective playoff races on Thanksgiving Day.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills and Chicago Bears picked up vital wins in their respective playoff races on Thanksgiving Day.

Buffalo's last-second win over the Kansas City Chiefs made it the first 10-win team in the NFL this season.

The win also provided the Bills with a valuable head-to-head tiebreaker if the Chiefs become their competition for the No. 1 seed.

Chicago's last-second heroics against the Detroit Lions put it a half-game behind the San Francisco 49ers in the NFC.

The 49ers are still the favorite to claim home-field advantage, but the Bears look like a very formidable challenger.

Buffalo's walk-off win over Kansas City allowed it to remain at least one game ahead of Denver at the top of the AFC.

The Broncos are likely to move to 9-2 on Friday with a win over the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Buffalo's win dropped Kansas City two games back of it. That gap really feels like a three-game advantage with the head-to-head tiebreaker.

That could be important in the coming weeks because Kansas City could easily move back to the top of the AFC West and challenge for home-field advantage.

Right now, the Chiefs are the top wild-card team ahead of the Cleveland Browns and the Steelers.

Kansas City should remain ahead of both of those teams in the coming weeks. The Chiefs' primary goal is to hunt down the Broncos atop the AFC West.

Chicago's thrilling last-second victory on the road in Detroit pushed it into first place in the NFC North.

The Bears are now just a half-game out of the No. 1 seed. The San Francisco 49ers host the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday.

A 49ers loss would put them and the Bears level on record at the end of Week 12.

At minimum, Chicago holds the upper hand in the NFC North title race over the Lions.

Detroit is still in good shape to make the playoffs with a 1.5-game cushion over the eighth-place Seahawks.

A Seahawks loss to the 49ers would benefit the Lions because that would then put a two-game gap between themselves and the teams outside the playoff positions.

The Philadelphia Eagles gained ground in the NFC East with their win over the Dallas Cowboys.

The New York Giants are still the clear favorite to claim the NFC East crown, but the recent wins by Philadelphia on Thanksgiving and the Washington Commanders on Monday night at least make things tighter in that race.

articles.title: Who won Bills vs Chiefs Thanksgiving game? Inside the dramatic final moments of Josh Allen vs Patrick Mahomes
articles.summary: Tyler Bass booted a 57-yard field goal as time ran out Thursday night, and the Buffalo Bills beat the Kansas City Chiefs 13-10 in a wet, ugly Thanksgiving
articles.body: Tyler Bass booted a 57-yard field goal as time ran out Thursday night, and the Buffalo Bills beat the Kansas City Chiefs 13-10 in a wet, ugly Thanksgiving game. Buffalo moves to 10-1. Kansas City falls to 8-3 and now faces a hard climb to the AFC's top seed. Josh Allen and Patrick Mahomes did not decide this one. Special teams did, with a tipped punt, a missed Chiefs kick and one long swing of Bass's leg. Bass had also tied it at 10-10 in the fourth quarter.Bills beat Chiefs 13-10 on Bass's last-second kickBuffalo led 7-3 at halftime, and the score said plenty about the conditions. Neither offense could get going. Kansas City took a 10-7 lead on its first drive of the third quarter, which ended a remarkable run for the Bills' defense. Buffalo had not allowed a touchdown since the opening quarter of its Week 8 win over Baltimore. That stretch covered 46 drives and tied the 2008 Ravens for the longest in the past 20 NFL seasons.Then the kickers took over.Bass tied the game with a 54-yarder. Harrison Butker answered with a miss from 46 yards. Buffalo punted, and rookie Tommy Doman Jr. sent it 57 yards, with Josh Downs forced out of bounds at the Kansas City 7. The Chiefs went three-and-out, but Matt Araiza's 38-yard punt was a poor one and gave the Bills the ball near midfield. They could not score, so Doman punted again, this time 46 yards. Kansas City started at its own 11 with 26 seconds left.The last punt decided it. Joe Andreessen got a hand on Araiza's kick, and Greg Dortch returned it 17 yards to the Kansas City 39. That left Bass a 57-yard try in bad weather. He made it.That is the odd part of this win. The Bills did not beat Kansas City with their best players. They beat the Chiefs with a rookie punter, a tipped ball and a kicker who needed 57 yards.Josh Allen's turnovers and the questions left for both teamsAllen threw two interceptions in the red zone. One bounced off Khalil Shakir's hands, so it is hard to pin entirely on the quarterback, though the throw was not clean either. Still, the numbers are getting harder to ignore. Allen has thrown an interception in five straight games, seven in all. The wet field explains some of Thursday. It does not explain the weeks before. With a tough run of games ahead, the habit matters more now.Buffalo's defense deserves credit, and it will still get an asterisk. During the touchdown-free streak it faced backup quarterbacks, and Mahomes was working in wet conditions. Fair or not, that is the criticism. The Bills can only play who is on the schedule.For Kansas City, the loss hurts in the standings. The Chiefs still have a path to the playoffs, but the No. 1 seed looks far away. This was the 11th meeting between Allen and Mahomes, and it may be the one that had the least to do with either of them.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Los Bills ganan a los Chiefs con un 'field goal' de 57 yardas con el tiempo agotado
articles.standfirst: Partido marcado por las duras condiciones climáticas
articles.summary: Partido marcado por las duras condiciones climáticas
articles.body: Los Buffalo Bills superaron el jueves de Acción de Gracias a los Kansas City Chiefs por 13-10 en un duelo marcado por las duras condiciones climáticas gracias a un 'field goal' de 57 yardas anotado cuando el tiempo ya se había agotado. El Bills-Chiefs puso el broche a una jornada de Acción de Gracias épica, con los tres partidos decididos en la última jugada tras las victorias de los Chicago Bears sobre los Detroit Lions y de los Philadelphia Eagles ante los Dallas Cowboys. Este último partido en Buffalo, que enfrentó a dos aspirantes al Super Bowl, se disputó bajo fuertes ráfagas de viento y lluvia incesante. El triunfo de los Bills, el séptimo consecutivo, les deja con un balance de 10-1, el mejor de toda la NFL. Los Chiefs, en cambio, caen a un 8-3, en la segunda plaza de la División Oeste de la Conferencia Nacional por detrás de los Denver Broncos. Los Bills se llevaron el triunfo pese a la discreta actuación de su mariscal de campo, Josh Allen, que apenas completó 10 de sus 21 pases -ninguno de 'touchdown'- para 81 yardas, con dos intercepciones. Patrick Mahomes, en cambio, completó 16 de sus 29 pases para 174 yardas, sin intercepciones, aunque, como Allen, no conectó ningún 'touchdown'. La lluvia y el viento convirtieron el partido de Buffalo en una auténtica batalla: 12 de los 20 'drives' terminaron en despeje 'punt'. Los Bills se adelantaron en el segundo cuarto con un 'touchdown' de James Cook III, al que los Chiefs solo pudieron responder antes del descanso con un 'field goal'. 7-3 y a vestuarios. Los Chiefs le dieron la vuelta al marcador en el tercer cuarto con un 'touchdown' de Emmett Johnson. Como el de los Bills, llegó en una carrera, desde la zona roja. Ya en el último cuarto, el pateador Tyler Bass puso el empate (10-10) con un 'field goal' de 54 yardas. Los Chiefs tuvieron la oportunidad de adelantarse de nuevo, pero Harrison Butker falló un intento desde 46 yardas, el octavo que falla esta temporada. Los cuatro siguientes 'drive' acabaron en nada, hasta que Buffalo se hizo con la posesión con un puñado de segundos en el reloj. Bass, desde las 57 yardas, anotó su segundo 'field goal' de la noche para el 13-10, saliendo como el héroe del partido.

articles.title: Andy Reid disagrees with overturned Rashee Rice catch after Chiefs' loss to Bills: 'That was not clear and obvious'
articles.summary: We may never know what a catch is in the NFL.
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice appeared to have a much-needed first down against the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving. The NFL's replay center disagreed.

With the game tied 10-10 and two minutes left in the fourth quarter, the Chiefs got the ball deep in their own territory. A pair of incompletions left them facing third-and-10, at which point Patrick Mahomes appeared to connect with wide receiver Rashee Rice for 11 yards and the first down.

However, the play was surprisingly overturned on replay, with the official only saying, "After review, the ball hit the ground, it's an incomplete pass."

The call was popular at Buffalo's Highmark Stadium, but not so much on social media.

The video replay indeed showed the ball hit the ground while pinned between Rice's right hand and shoulder, but that alone doesn't make the play an incomplete pass. The ball must also come loose while hitting the ground before Rice establishes possession, and that was very much up for debate.

Additionally, the NFL maintains a "clear and obvious" standard for overturning plays. So the replay officials in New York City not only believed Rice hadn't completed the catch, they also decided it was clear to anyone watching.

Chiefs head coach Andy Reid very much didn't seem to think that was the case after his team's 13-10 defeat , via Kansas City's KSHB 41 :

"Not [a call] that I agreed with, but yeah. This came from New York, so it's not from these guys. Our guys called it a completion, the guys who were working the game. I'm not quite sure what they saw. I saw he had control of the ball and his elbow hit and then the ball hit, but he had control. "Normally, in those kind of situations, it's gotta be clear and obvious. To me, that was not clear and obvious."

"Not [a call] that I agreed with, but yeah. This came from New York, so it's not from these guys. Our guys called it a completion, the guys who were working the game. I'm not quite sure what they saw. I saw he had control of the ball and his elbow hit and then the ball hit, but he had control.

"Normally, in those kind of situations, it's gotta be clear and obvious. To me, that was not clear and obvious."

Mahomes' wife Brittany, meanwhile, used the occasion to dispute the idea the Chiefs have benefited from calls during their recent run, writing the following on her Instagram story :

"HAHAHAHAHAHA WHAT A JOKE "Guess we can't even play football without getting it called against us… not sure what an actual catch is after that I guess? I don't wanna hear s*** anymore from anyone"

"Guess we can't even play football without getting it called against us… not sure what an actual catch is after that I guess? I don't wanna hear s*** anymore from anyone"

She also posted a collection of social media posts criticizing the call to her story.

NFL vice president of instant replay Mark Butterworth spoke to a pool reporter, pointing to Rice's hand moving up the ball as evidence that he lost control.

To be clear, this play did not singlehandedly cost the Chiefs the game, though it's undeniably frustrating. Had the Rice catch stood, they still would have needed to travel half the field to reach field-goal range, on a day in which struggling kicker Harrison Butker made one field goal from 26 yards and missed another from 46.

Facing fourth-and-10, Kansas City was instead forced to punt out of its own end zone. The teams immediately exchanged three-and-outs and appeared headed to overtime, only for field position to bite the Chiefs again when a disastrous punt sequence put the Bills in field-goal position for the final play.

articles.title: Steelers’ Aaron Rodgers Exit Opens Door for Potential ‘Nostalgia Move’ in NFC
articles.summary: Following his departure from the Steelers, Aaron Rodgers was floated as a potential signing for the team he grew up rooting for. The post Steelers’ Aaron Rod...
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers is officially a free agent after his rather ugly departure from the Pittsburgh Steelers. And if the four-time NFL MVP wants to play football again this season, he could have an opportunity to do something he's wanted to do since he was a kid.

Rodgers cleared waivers Thursday, a day after the Steelers released him following his public criticism of head coach Mike McCarthy on ESPN's "The Pat McAfee Show."

No team was willing to take on the remainder of Rodgers' contract with Pittsburgh, but any interested team can now negotiate a new deal with the 42-year-old quarterback.

Among the destinations being floated for Rodgers is the very team that passed on him more than 21 years ago.

Aaron Rodgers Floated for Nostalgia Move to 49ers

CBS Sports' Bryan DeArdo included the San Francisco 49ers among his potential landing spots for Rodgers, even though they already have one of the NFL's best quarterbacks this season.

"This is mostly a nostalgia move. Rodgers is a California native who grew up a diehard 49ers fan. The 49ers famously passed on him in the 2005 NFL Draft, and Rodgers has never been shy about his desire to show his childhood team they made a big mistake."

Rodgers grew up in Northern California and played two seasons at Cal before entering the NFL draft. The 49ers took Utah quarterback Alex Smith with the No. 1 overall pick, leaving Rodgers to fall to the Green Bay Packers at No. 24.

Ironically, the team Rodgers grew up rooting for was responsible for ending four of his postseason runs in Green Bay. He went 0-4 against San Francisco in the playoffs as the Packers' starting quarterback, including a loss in the NFC championship game following the 2019 season.

The 49ers had an opportunity to revisit their draft decision in 2021. Head coach Kyle Shanahan contacted Packers head coach Matt LaFleur about Rodgers' availability ahead of that year's draft, but Green Bay wasn't interested in moving its quarterback.

The 49ers instead selected Trey Lance with the No. 3 overall pick.

49ers Dealing With QB Injury After Aaron Rodgers' Release

DeArdo's suggestion came with the understanding that Rodgers would be playing behind Brock Purdy in San Francisco, something he hasn't done as a healthy quarterback since his days backing up Brett Favre in Green Bay.

"In this scenario, Rodgers would have the chance to go home and play for his childhood team, albeit in a backup role. He also could serve as a mentor for Brock Purdy, who is having an MVP-caliber season. Given the 49ers' injury history, Kyle Shanahan probably wouldn't mind having a backup with Rodgers' experience."

Interestingly enough, Purdy has missed consecutive practices this week with a sprained ankle, leaving his availability for Sunday's game against the Seattle Seahawks in question. Mac Jones would be in line to start if Purdy can't play, with Kurtis Rourke behind him.

Purdy was named NFC Offensive Player of the Week for the second time this season after throwing for 255 yards and three touchdowns in a 35-10 victory over the Minnesota Vikings in Mexico City. The win improved San Francisco to 9-1.

Rodgers started 10 games for Pittsburgh this season, throwing for 2,241 yards and 16 touchdowns. If he were to join the 49ers, he'd be going from a team trying to hold onto a playoff spot to one that has a chance to get him back to the Super Bowl for the first time in 16 seasons.

articles.title: Bills HC Joe Brady applauds Buffalo for finding ways to win on Josh Allen’s off night
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills didn’t need a vintage Josh Allen performance to take down the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving night, and head coach Joe Brady couldn’t...
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills didn't need a vintage Josh Allen performance to take down the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving night , and head coach Joe Brady couldn't be prouder of how his team found a way.

After the game, Brady pointed to the gritty victory as a sign of what his team is made of.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"To win a game like this when Josh Allen had 80 passing yards says a lot about our football team," Brady said, via Matthew Bove.

Allen completed just 10 of his 21 passes for a season-low 81 yards with no touchdowns, two interceptions and an 18.3 passer rating. Both picks came in the red zone, with safeties Alohi Gilman and Nohl Williams snuffing out what could have been scoring opportunities for Buffalo.

It was the second straight game in which Allen threw two interceptions . The star quarterback was quick to take accountability. "I have to be better; I need to be better; I will be better. Thankful for my team," he said.

Fortunately for the Bills, the rest of the roster picked up the slack. James Cook carried the load on the ground, piling up 117 rushing yards and a touchdown on 32 carries. As a team, Buffalo ran the ball 43 times and controlled the clock for nearly 37 minutes.

The defense also held up its end of the bargain, limiting Patrick Mahomes to 16-of-29 passing for 174 yards and no touchdowns.

Bass then delivered in the clutch. After tying the game with a 54-yarder early in the fourth quarter, he drilled the game-winner to send the home crowd into a frenzy.

The win extended Buffalo's winning streak to seven games and improved its record to 10-1, keeping the Bills in sole possession of the AFC's top spot.

articles.title: Bills QB Josh Allen Makes Promise to His Team After Poor Performance Against Chiefs
articles.summary: Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen vowed to improve after a poor game against the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving. The post Bills QB Josh Allen Makes Pr...
articles.body:
Buffalo Bills quarterback Josh Allen escaped Thursday's game against the Kansas City Chiefs with a win — an ugly one.

Allen threw two interceptions, but got some huge plays from Buffalo's special teams to lead up to a walkoff field goal from Tyler Bass.

After the game, Allen got brutally hones about his poor performance.

Speaking to reporters after the Thanksgiving win, Allen admitted that he played a terrible game and said he needs to improve for the sake of his team.

"I have to be better. I will be better," Allen said, via reporter Matthew Bove.

Allen completed just 10 of 21 passes for 81 yards and two interceptions, also taking two sacks for a net loss of 17 yards.

Bove noted that Allen acknowledged the poor weather conditions, some of the worst the Bills have played in across his career.

"Allen went on to say he hasn't played well for two games. Said it was one of the worst weather games he's played in but it's not an excuse because everyone had to play in it," Bove noted.

articles.title: Cowboys’ Dak Prescott Addresses Coaching Change After Thanksgiving Loss
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys lost again in stunning fashion on Thanksgiving. Dak Prescott was asked about what it means for Brian Schottenheimer. The post Cowboys’ Dak...
articles.body:
It's been an odd week for the two most recent Dallas Cowboys coaches, but the running theme has been change. Mike McCarthy is dealing with his fair share of questions and upheaval in Pittsburgh, but he still has his team well-positioned for the playoffs, which is a lot more than Brian Schottenheimer can say. Schottenheimer replaced McCarthy as Cowboys coach a little less than two years ago in what now looks like a disastrous decision, as Schottenheimer's record fell to 5-7 this season and 12-16-1 overall in his time as coach with another massive blown lead (it was 31-10 late in the third quarter) for what quarterback Dak Prescott called a "stunning" 39-38 loss to the Eagles.

Schottenheimer got a vote of confidence from owner Jerry Jones after the game, which is not a big surprise–Jones does not like the idea of replacing coaches midseason. But there does not seem to be much reason to maintain that confidence in Schottenheimer this year.

Dak Prescott: 'I Don't Know' About Brian Schottenheimer Status

Prescott himself addressed the possibility of Schottenheimer getting fired by the Cowboys in the coming days or weeks. He played dumb, which can likely be seen as an acknowledgement that Schottenheimer is not going anywhere. It's unlikely that Schottenheimer will give up play-calling duties, as he forced defensive coordinator Christian Parker to do last week.

Prescott was asked specifically about "if there were to be a change, anywhere, on the coaching staff" but was reluctant to throw Schottenheimer under any buses: "I don't know what you're alluding to, so, I am gonna focus on doing what I can, the best I can, and controlling what I can and handle whatever comes as it comes. As I do in life."

It was a well-placed dodge for Prescott, who leads the NFL in passing yards.

Prescott was more open in discussing his feelings about the loss: "Pretty stunning. I guess I said it a couple of weeks ago after the Arizona game how stunning that was. But this one takes the cake. Division opponent. Division rival. That's how these games come down, they come down to the wire. They made more plays."

The Cowboys will be off more than a week, as they do not play again until December 7, against the Seahawks on the road on Monday night football.

articles.title: Bills’ Fan Favorite ‘Buffalo Joe’ Delivers Thanksgiving Miracle Against Chiefs
articles.summary: Buffalo Bills fan favorite LB Joe Andreessen delivered Thanksgiving miracle against Chiefs. The post Bills’ Fan Favorite ‘Buffalo Joe’ Delivers Thanksgiving...
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills just needed a little local flavor — and a little local magic — to cap off Thanksgiving Day with a 13-10 walk-off win over the Kansas City Chiefs at the new Highmark Stadium.

In the end, fan favorite linebacker and local product Joe Andreessen — who grew up just 18 miles from the stadium — came through with a blocked punt in the pouring rain to set up a game-winning 57-yard field goal by Tyler Bass as time expired.

"Buffalo Joe comes through," NBC color commentator Cris Collinsworth said on the broadcast.

"'Buffalo Joe' Andreessen helps set up the game-winner by getting his hands on the punt!" Buffalo Sports Talk wrote on its official X account. "What a moment. What a win."

The Bills improved to 10-1 with the win — their 7th straight win.

Bills Just Signed Andreessen to Contract Extension

The Bills signed Andreessen to a 2-year, $3 million contract extension on October 3.

Andreesen, 6-foot-1 and 240 pounds, made the Bills roster as an undrafted free agent in 2024 after earning FCS All-American honors at Bryant in 2022 before transferring to the University of Buffalo for his final season in 2023.

Andreessen Earned Famous Nickname From Allen

Andreessen, 6-foot-1 and 240 pounds, made the Bills roster on the strength of his play in the 2024 preseason and earned an all-time nickname from NFL MVP quarterback Josh Allen — Buffalo Joe.

"Andreessen is far beyond a cute story at this point, as he is legitimately one of the best special teams players in the NFL," SB Nation's Sean Murphy wrote on July 29. "He is a far more dynamic athlete than many people realize, as he is fast (4.64-second 40-yard dash, 4.22-second 20-yard shuttle), strong (32 reps of 225 pounds on the bench press), and explosive (38″ vertical and 10'2″ broad jump). His Relative Athletic Score, or RAS, was a 9.35 based on his Pro Day results. In short, Andreessen is a dynamic athlete, not just some local kid living out a dream."

articles.title: Lions’ Kerby Joseph knows who’s to blame for Rome Odunze dagger TD
articles.summary: The Detroit Lions let a golden opportunity slip away on Thanksgiving, and Kerby Joseph isn’t pointing fingers at anyone but his own unit after Rome Odunze’s...
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions let a golden opportunity slip away on Thanksgiving, and Kerby Joseph isn't pointing fingers at anyone but his own unit after Rome Odunze 's game-winning touchdown sealed a stunning Chicago Bears comeback.

The Bears stormed back from an 11-point fourth-quarter deficit to beat the Lions 39-35 at Ford Field. Caleb Williams capped a 13-play, 68-yard drive by finding Odunze for a 6-yard touchdown in the final seconds, with the replay official upholding the catch.

After the game, Joseph took responsibility on behalf of the defense. "It's hard. Last play again, and it's on the defense. We just gotta be better as a whole, and we will be, especially after this. I'm not gonna say we needed this, but it's a good eye-opener," he said, via 97.1 The Ticket.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Detroit appeared to be in control after Jahmyr Gibbs broke loose for a 70-yard touchdown run with 8:30 remaining , giving the Lions a 35-24 lead. But Chicago answered about a minute later, with Williams hitting Odunze for a 41-yard score before converting the two-point try himself to make it a three-point game.

The Lions had a chance to put the game away, but Bears linebacker T.J. Edwards stopped Gibbs short on a fourth-and-4 completion to keep Chicago within striking distance.

It was a frustrating result for a Detroit offense that piled up 549 total yards, including 246 on the ground. Even so, the defense had no answer for Williams, who completed 30 of 44 passes for 345 yards and two touchdowns without an interception.

Odunze was the star of the fourth quarter, hauling in both of Chicago's touchdown passes in the period, including the dagger.

The loss snapped Detroit's six-game winning streak and dropped the Lions to 8-3. More importantly, it gave the 9-2 Bears a one-game cushion atop the NFC North.

Joseph's message suggests the Lions are taking the defeat as motivation rather than a reason to panic. With a rematch in Chicago set for Jan. 3, Detroit will get a chance to settle the score.

Before that, the Lions will hit the road to face the Atlanta Falcons on Dec. 6.

articles.title: Legendary Ex-Bills WR Makes ‘Rigged’ Allegation After Controversial Rashee Rice Call
articles.summary: Former Buffalo Bills wide receiver Terrell Owens blasted a call against the Kansas City Chiefs in their loss to the Bills on Thanksgiving night. The post Leg...
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs lost a heartbreaker to the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving night, and a controversial call against receiver Rashee Rice is pouring some salt in the wounds.

The Chiefs receiver appeared to make a critical first-down conversion late in the fourth quarter, but officials reviewed the play and determined that the ball hit the ground when he was tackled. The Chiefs were forced to punt, then lost after a pair of possession changes.

The call led to an uproar, with even a legendary former Bills wide receiver suggesting the Chiefs were robbed.

Bills Receiver Makes 'Rigged' Allegation

After the call, former Bills receiver Terrell Owens said it appeared clear to him that Rice held on the ball as he was knocked to the ground.

"If that wasn't a catch, NOTHING is," Owens wrote in a post on X . "And I'm actually barracking for my Buffalo Bills!!! But these calls by refs are beyond ridiculous. This is why people are talking about games being rigged."

Others joined Owens in lamenting the call. Former NFL quarterback turned analyst Robert Griffin III said it appeared to be a clear catch.

"Chiefs fans HAVE EVERY REASON TO BE UPSET. THAT WAS A CATCH BY RASHEE RICE," Griffin shared in a post on X .

The Chiefs punted, then held the Bills to a three-and-out, but failed to gain any yards on their next drive. Bills special teams ace Joe Andreessen partially blocked Matt Ariaza's punt and returner Greg Dortch returned it to the 40-yard line, leading to a walk-off field goal from Tyler Bass.

articles.title: The Dead Cap Won't Impact The Cleveland Browns Decision On Deshaun Watson
articles.summary: Here is Deshaun Watson's current five year contract. Each years cash is shown in a different color so you can see how the salary cap is managed. He is paid t...
articles.body:
Here is Deshaun Watson's current five year contract. Each years cash is shown in a different color so you can see how the salary cap is managed. He is paid this cash during the year, so there is no money to pay beyond the final game of the 2026 regular season.

In December 2024, the Cleveland Browns asked Deshaun Watson's camp to amend his contract. This was to allow them to 'extend' his contract by a few days so that he could be a Post June 1st cut in March 2027 rather than becoming a free agent two days earlier. This means they can split the 2027 dead cap across the 2027 and 2028 season.

The mechanism to do this is either called adding a dummy year or adding a poison pill clause into the contract. It says if he is on the team on the 13th March 2027 they will guarantee him $200m in the 2029 season. He is never going to see this money but it just gives him certainty they will be cutting him.

Here are the changes/impact for all sides:

Watson - he is a free agent two/three days later and can't be franchise tagged (that is set to be over $50m next year, he is never going to get that)

Browns - they can split his dead cap over two years but they lose the ability for Watson to qualify as part of the comp pick formula (they aren't likely to get any anyway as they will add more free agents than lose them)

The Cleveland Browns are likely to select a quarterback in the first round of the 2027 NFL Draft, the consensus big board currently has eight quarterbacks going in the first round. So if they are adding a veteran quarterback it is likely a bridge who will play as long as they are competitive or the rookie is ready.

Here is the market in 2026 for these type of quarterbacks: Top Backup, Justin Fields - $11m Top Bridge, Jacoby Brissett - $15.5m

Let's be overly optimistic and say he wins a playoff game, then you could look to beat this marked and potentially give him $20m for a year.

I expect them to put another dummy year/poison pill into the contract, this is what it does to the salary cap over the next three years: 2027 - Up $5,076,000 2028 - Down $23,098,000 2029 - Up $38,022,000

The extra $20m they have given him all lands on the salary cap still. It moves the salary cap up and down a little over the next three years but you are paying $20m for that. The question is, is Deshaun Watson worth the extra $20m, not what it does to the salary cap. While there is minor benefit, but your do make $20m quarterback decisions based on minor salary cap benefit.

For me the biggest factor in will Watson return comes down to what he does in the potential playoff game. If we see a Joe Flacco game like we did against the Texans with a 45-14 loss then it is hard to run it back. A win isn't everything, if they go close against a team like the Chiefs, Bills or Jaguars then the temptation will be to run it back.

The decision will be a big one for Andrew Berry. We have seen Kwesi Adofo-Mensah lose his job for not extending Sam Darnold. We have seen Chris Ballard lose his job for extending Daniel Jones. There is risk either way.

In my mind Todd Monken should have a significant say in the veteran quarterback decision, it is who he thinks he can get the most out of in the short term. The biggest Browns decision this offseason is which quarterback they draft. If next season sees regression but they draft the future of the franchise then the 2027 season will quickly be forgotten.

articles.title: Andy Reid Speaks Out on Controversial Rashee Rice Overturned Catch
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs lost a heartbreaker to the Buffalo Bills by a final score of 13-10 on Thanksgiving night. Despite consistently shooting themselves in...
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs lost a heartbreaker to the Buffalo Bills by a final score of 13-10 on Thanksgiving night.

Despite consistently shooting themselves in the foot with miscues, the Chiefs had two possession late in the fourth quarter with a chance to take the lead or force overtime. One play in particular went against them that was not their fault.

Kansas City Chiefs HC Andy Reid Disagrees With Overturned Catch by WR Rashee Rice

During a third-and-10 situation backed up on their own nine-yard line, quarterback Patrick Mahomes completed a pass to wide receiver Rashee Rice across the middle of the field for a first down. However, to everybody's surprise, the call was overturned to an incomplete pass .

That sparked a ton of controversy on social media and will certainly be a focal point of conversation over the next week. Coach Andy Reid spoke on the ruling after the game, and made his feelings on the decision crystal clear.

"Not one that I agree with," Reid said of the overturned call. "They said it came from New York. It wasn't from our guys (the referees), they called it a completion. I'm not quite sure what they saw. I saw he had control of the ball, then his elbow hit, then the ball hit, but he had control. Normally in those situations, it has to be clear and obvious. To me, that was not clear and obvious."

NFL Continues to Struggle Defining a Catch

After Rice's catch was overturned to an incompletion, the Chiefs punted. Kansas City's defense was able to get the ball back to the offense, but it failed to capitalize. The Bills went on to hit the game-winning field goal as time expired.

Had the play not have been overruled, the Chiefs would have had a fresh set of downs with 1:41 left to go. Who knows what would have happened from there, but they certainly had the momentum and could have taken some more time off the clock.

The NFL frustratingly has had a handful of calls every season like this for decades. It has failed to clearly determine what constitutes a catch , with explanations being inconsistent. Kansas City has now fallen to 8-3 on the season, and the Bills are in firm control of the AFC at 10-1.

articles.title: In October 2026, Joe Milton was on the Dallas Cowboys' practice squad; 41 days later, he led the Philadelphia Eagles to the biggest Thanksgiving comeback in NFL history against his former team
articles.summary: Joe Milton was a Cowboys practice squad quarterback in October.
articles.body: Joe Milton was a Cowboys practice squad quarterback in October. On Thanksgiving night in Arlington, he beat Dallas, his former team, from the other sideline. Playing for the Philadelphia Eagles, Milton threw for 331 yards and three touchdowns, ran for another score and led a rally from 21 points down. Jake Elliott's 59-yard field goal with two seconds left made it 39-38, the biggest comeback in Thanksgiving history in NFL games. It was only Milton's third career start, and it came after Dallas cut him following training camp.How a former Cowboys practice squad passer beat Dallas on ThanksgivingJoe Milton did not need a perfect pocket for this one. Philadelphia trailed 21-3 late in the second quarter when he slid away from pressure, spotted DeVonta Smith one-on-one downfield and let it go for a 50-yard touchdown. Next Gen Stats tracked the ball at 64.4 yards in the air once the angle was counted. Milton said his first read was blocked by a linebacker and his second drifted too far away. So he escaped, looked up and trusted his arm. Smith had told him the week before to trust him on 50-50 balls.The second Smith score came late in the third quarter, a 45-yarder off play action after Milton rolled right, away from Kenny Clark. That made it 31-17. Smith ended with a career-high 200 yards on 11 catches and two touchdowns, even after getting banged up. Milton completed 21 of 31 passes for 331 yards, with three touchdown throws, one interception and a rushing touchdown. No Eagles quarterback had thrown two touchdowns of 45-plus yards in one game since Carson Wentz in 2019.He was named the game's MVP, then took his time leaving. Milton ate turkey on the field and walked into the locker room with a glass turkey-leg trophy almost 15 minutes after the final whistle. Coach Nick Sirianni, waiting to give his postgame speech, joked that someone should ask FOX analyst Tom Brady to let the Eagles have their quarterback back.The 21-point hole, the blocked punt and the final 50 secondsFor three quarters, this looked like a Dallas win. The Cowboys led 31-10 and still had a 14-point cushion early in the fourth. Philadelphia was thin, too. Jalen Hurts was out, and running back Saquon Barkley left in the first quarter with a stinger.Special teams cracked it open. Ty Robinson blocked a Bryan Anger punt, and Kenny Moore II scooped it up and ran it in to make it 31-24. Dak Prescott answered with a rushing touchdown for 38-24 with 10:19 left. Milton kept chipping away. Down eight inside 2:30, he took a shotgun snap, rolled right past two blitzers and hit Makai Lemon in the back of the end zone. That cut it to two.Then Robinson struck again, sacking Prescott on a fourth-down play. Philadelphia took over at its own 48 with 50 seconds left and no timeouts. Milton missed Darius Cooper, found Smith for nine, drew a pass interference flag on a throw toward Zach Ertz, then connected with Smith for five more. A false start on Markel Bell pushed them back, but it was close enough. Elliott's kick from 59 yards sailed through. Dallas fell to 5-7, and the pressure on coach Brian Schottenheimer grew.Why the Eagles built their offense around Milton's armMilton's road here was messy. The New England Patriots took him in the sixth round in 2024, and Dallas traded for him in April 2025. He spent last season as a backup, then was cut after this summer's training camp and signed to the practice squad. Philadelphia saw an opening in mid-October. Hurts was dealing with blood clots, Andy Dalton had left, and Tanner McKee's rough outings made a change easy to justify. By Week 9 Milton was starting. He is the fourth Eagles quarterback to throw a pass this year.The Eagles adjusted, too. After the bye they moved away from under-center snaps and leaned on shotgun and pistol looks that suit his mobility and arm. Milton, 26, says he has worked for years with quarterback coach Donovan Dooley on throws made on the run, the exact skill behind the Lemon touchdown. His escapability was a big reason the coaches picked him over McKee in the first place. He prefers the nickname Mr. Rocket to Bazooka Joe, though nobody in Philadelphia was arguing about labels on Thursday.Teammates talked about his composure more than his arm. “The guy is a rock star, man,” Jordan Mailata said. Receiver Elijah Moore added that Milton takes over the huddle without wavering.What the win means for Joe Milton and a patchwork Eagles seasonMilton kept his own reading modest. He said he does not know what the game does for his career, only that the team played well and his confidence is up. He also said he was thankful, both to the Eagles and for the chance he had on Dallas' scout team.Some caution fits. Dallas has the league's worst defense, as the Inquirer noted, which matters when judging a 331-yard night. The Eagles' offense is also a patchwork right now. Hurts is out, Barkley was hurt, and tight end Dallas Goedert and cornerback Cooper DeJean both left early.Then there is Milton's future. Will Philadelphia want him back, and in what role? Will another team see this game and wonder if it can last? Those answers start in Arizona, where the Eagles head for Week 13. A fourth start there will tell more than any Thanksgiving highlight.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
