articles.title: Week 12 Waiver Wire Pickups and Available Sleepers in Most Yahoo and Sleeper Leagues
articles.summary: We're already two days and four games into Week 12. Many of the week's top waiver options have been off the board for some time, though some managers may still be seeking help.
articles.body:
We're already two days and four games into Week 12. Many of the week's top waiver options have been off the board for some time, though some managers may still be seeking help.

While all 32 teams are in action this week, injuries continue to leave fantasy stars on the sidelines.

Here, we'll examine some Week 12 sleepers who may still be available in your league heading into the weekend. These players are still rostered in fewer than 50 percent of Yahoo and Sleeper leagues and have intriguing value, particularly in point-per-reception (PPR) formats.

As a reminder, the week will pick back up with the Pittsburgh Steelers and Denver Broncos at 3 p.m. ET on Friday. Make sure to adjust your lineups accordingly.

Deshaun Watson's inconsistent play makes him difficult to trust in fantasy. However, the Cleveland Browns quarterback carries a fair bit of upside into Week 12.

The Browns have struggled to run the ball effectively, which has led to Watson using his legs more in competitive games—he didn't do much running (or much of anything) in the blowout loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers in Week 8.

Two weeks ago, Watson recorded 22.4 fantasy points. He and the Browns were on bye last week and have had extra time to prepare for a Las Vegas Raiders defense that has struggled.

Las Vegas has surrendered the fifth-most fantasy points to opposing quarterbacks this season. Watson is still available in roughly 80 percent of fantasy leagues.

Everyone knows that Derrick Henry leads the Baltimore Ravens' rushing attack. If you haven't watched the Ravens recently, though, you may have missed Justice Hill's increasing role as a complementary receiving back.

Hill has averaged four receptions per game over the past four weeks, and he has reached double-digit fantasy points in two of his last four. Against the Carolina Panthers last week, he also ran for 89 yards and finished with 17.6 fantasy points.

Having logged no fewer than seven fantasy points over the past month, Hill should have a solid floor against the Houston Texans this week. Houston has fielded a middle-of-the-pack defense against the run, surrendering an average of 18.5 fantasy points to opposing backfields.

Hill is still only rostered in 29 percent of fantasy leagues.

Antonio Williams, WR, Washington Commanders

Even if you aren't hurting at wide receiver, Antonio Williams is worth a waiver claim. He morphed into Jayden Daniels' go-to target last Monday night, and he's likely to maintain the quarterback's confidence moving forward.

Williams was the target on both of Daniels' passes during the Washington Commanders' final, game-winning drive. He helped Washington upset the Cincinnati Bengals, and he likely delivered a win to many fantasy managers along the way.

On Monday, Williams caught nine of 11 targets and finished with 21.2 fantasy points. He may not see that volume against a bad Arizona Cardinals team this week, but Arizona has surrendered the 10th-most fantasy points to opposing receivers.

While Williams was heavily targeted early in the week, he's still available in over 60 percent of fantasy leagues.

If you missed the big news of the week, Aaron Rodgers is no longer the Steelers' starting quarterback. In fact, he's not even a Steeler anymore, as Pittsburgh cut him on Wednesday.

It'll be Mason Rudolph behind center for now, and the career backup should look to rely heavily on tight end Pat Freiermuth this week. The Steelers will likely look to give Rudolph quick, easy completions against a ferocious Denver Broncos pass rush, and Freiermuth has traditionally been a terrific safety outlet.

Last week, Freiermuth caught five of five targets and finished with nine fantasy points. He could be targeted twice that many times on Friday against a Broncos defense that has been beaten by tight ends.

Denver has surrendered the fourth-most fantasy points to the position. Freiermuth is still available in roughly 60 percent of leagues.

*Fantasy scoring and roster information from FantasyPros .

articles.title: Quarterback Trust Meter for All 32 NFL Teams Entering the Home Stretch
articles.summary: With Thanksgiving here, the NFL season has officially hit the home stretch.
articles.body:
With Thanksgiving here, the NFL season has officially hit the home stretch.

So, how confident are you in your team's quarterback?

Right now, 11 teams are rolling with someone other than their original starter. In a handful of those cases, the Week 1 QB1 has landed on injured reserve. Elsewhere, benchings, releases and trades have triggered major shake-ups atop the depth chart.

Focusing on each team's current starter—plus injured options who aren't on IR, such as Carson Beck—let's gauge how much every franchise should trust its quarterback situation with December approaching.

Here's a breakdown on a scale of 1 to 10.

He's an iron man, a former MVP and a leading contender for the award again in his prime. However, entering Week 12, only four quarterbacks had higher turnover-worthy play rates at Pro Football Focus . Combine that gunslinger risk with his past playoff failures, and he falls short of a perfect score.

Just two appearances into his career, the sophomore sixth-round pick has struggled mightily with very little support as the interim starter. Nobody is under the impression that he can be relied on beyond a pinch. The Dolphins are just waiting for Malik Willis to get healthy and resume his quest to become the guy.

New England Patriots — Tommy DeVito: 2/10

In three appearances so far, Drake Maye's temporary replacement has completed just 50 percent of his passes and posted a sub-60 passer rating. The undrafted 28-year-old had a moment with the Giants a few years ago but can't be trusted with regular reps in a playoff race.

I didn't see this coming, but Smith has not been the problem in New York. The league's seventh-highest-rated qualified passer has the third-best on-target rate among quarterbacks listed in this exercise. He's one of just four regular starters this year with a turnover-worthy play rate below 2.0 percent. He's not quite a franchise quarterback at age 36, but he's playing like a top-notch bridge.

Baltimore Ravens — Jacoby Brissett: 3/10

Only three quarterbacks listed here have lower qualified passer ratings than Brissett's (80.0). His sub-50 third-down passer rating ranks dead last among qualified signal-callers. The soon-to-be 34-year-old is just serving as a stopgap until Lamar Jackson returns.

Burrow has put together an MVP-caliber campaign so far. He's got a league-best 125.6 passer rating on deep attempts as well as the league's top qualified rating in the fourth quarter of one-score games . It really comes down to whether he can stay healthy and deliver in the playoffs. We haven't seen him in the postseason since 2022.

Watson has revived his career to the extent that he's now a mid-tier starter. The 31-year-old has delivered just one triple-digit-rated passing performance this season. He ranks in the bottom 10 in completed air yards per attempt as well as on-target rate, but he's limited his mistakes with mediocre support.

Pittsburgh Steelers — Mason Rudolph: 2/10

The team's decision to bench and then release Aaron Rodgers has shaken the football world, but that clearly didn't have too much to do with Rudolph. The 31-year-old has a mere 84.3 career passer rating and has generated just two passing yards on four attempts this season. Don't expect him to pull a Sam Darnold. Rudolph is a mistake-prone career backup in an awkward spot here.

Stroud has certainly bounced back, posting 22 touchdowns to four interceptions as the league's sixth-highest-rated qualified passer. That said, the 25-year-old still has to prove that he can come through when it matters. This is a guy who committed seven turnovers in two postseason games last year.

Indianapolis Colts — Anthony Richardson Sr.: 2/10

The 24-year-old takes over for Daniel Jones despite having thrown more career interceptions (13) than touchdown passes (11). The good news is this is an audition. A bad Indianapolis team won't need him for much other than due diligence for the rest of the way. It wouldn't be surprising if we also saw Riley Leonard at some point.

Jacksonville Jaguars — Trevor Lawrence: 7/10

Under Liam Coen's tutelage, Lawrence has finally become the player we were once promised. In his last 17 starts (the equivalent of one full regular season), the former top pick has gone 14-3 with 40 touchdown passes, 11 interceptions and a 106.6 passer rating. There are valid concerns. He has just a 75.8 passer rating in three career playoff starts and has struggled this year in key road games against Denver and the Giants. He also leads the AFC with a turnover-worthy play rate of 5.9 percent.

The second-year No. 1 overall pick might be playing the best football of his career right now. If he keeps it up, he could extinguish any chatter that his job could be in jeopardy this offseason. Still, the 24-year-old has yet to earn the benefit of the doubt and has a long way to go.

1 Thing Every NFL Fanbase Should Be Thankful For 🙏

It is alarming that Nix's rate-based numbers have dropped for a second consecutive season. Did he peak as a rookie? He's got a sub-60 completion percentage and an 83.3 passer rating. No bueno. That said, Nix continues to earn a reputation for getting it done in clutch situations, highlighted by a triple-digit rating in the fourth quarter of one-score games this season and 10 fourth-quarter comebacks since the start of 2025.

Kansas City Chiefs — Patrick Mahomes: 10/10

He's back! One of the most clutch quarterbacks in NFL history entered Week 12 as the league's third-highest-rated qualified passer and has a 120.3 rating in the fourth quarter of one-score games. He doesn't hit home runs as often as he used to, but there's nobody you'd rather have with a game on the line in January or February.

Las Vegas Raiders — Fernando Mendoza: 4/10

Obviously, the rookie No. 1 overall pick remains very green, but he hit on several deep balls in an encouraging Week 11 performance against Denver. The trajectory is promising. It'll just take time.

Los Angeles Chargers — Justin Herbert: 2/10

Yeesh. The veteran has a 40.2 passer rating on deep attempts, which is easily the worst among regular starters. He also has a sub-30 rating in the fourth quarter of one-score games. He's fallen off a cliff at age 28 in a lost season.

The 33-year-old has put up some huge numbers thus far in his 11th season, but there's a good reason he lacks a big-moment reputation. He's been OK at best in the fourth quarter of one-score games this year, as he's won just two playoff games in his career.

McCarthy has, at the very least, managed the offense effectively and reliably while making considerable progress in a new setting. Still, the 23-year-old's numbers aren't pretty. The sample size remains small for a guy who was a complete bust in Minnesota.

The 26-year-old quasi-journeyman is supposedly just a placeholder. Before Week 12, he had made two poor starts as the Eagles seemed to be playing out the string. However, he flashed serious upside while leading Philadelphia to an incredible comeback victory over Dallas on Thanksgiving. We shouldn't overreact to one game, but there could be something there.

Washington Commanders — Jayden Daniels: 7/10

He's actually been pretty good when healthy. We've seen what he can do with his arm and legs in critical games. Daniels is still a work in progress, but he's been smart with the football. If the Commanders fall short, it likely won't be on him unless he can't stay on the field.

"Iceman" was clutch again with a perfect go-ahead touchdown pass with three seconds left to beat the Lions in Detroit on Thanksgiving. He entered that game with a 108.0 passer rating in the fourth quarter of one-score games this season. He led the league with six fourth-quarter comebacks in 2025. Williams isn't a superstar yet, but he's close. That said, he loses some credit here for throwing five interceptions in two playoff games last year.

It helps that the veteran is surrounded by elite weapons and pass protectors, but that doesn't entirely explain how Goff is the NFC's highest-rated passer since the start of 2024. The problem is he has really struggled in his last two playoff losses and wasn't good with the season on the line last December.

The raw numbers are again strong, but I just don't know that Love has "it." Even before throwing two killer second-half interceptions Wednesday night in Los Angeles, he was one of the league's lowest-rated qualified passers in the fourth quarter of one-score games. He's also lost each of his last three playoff starts, although support has admittedly been an issue.

Among quarterbacks in this exercise, only Burrow has a higher third-down passer rating than Cousins (118.9), who has 11 touchdowns to one interception in those scenarios. He's truly having a strong year at age 38, but it's too early in his second stint with Minnesota to tell if he can be relied on down the stretch. He hasn't been part of a playoff victory since 2019.

Atlanta Falcons — Michael Penix Jr.: 2/10

It's just not working. Despite plenty of offensive support, the third-year first-round pick is a bottom-10-rated passer trending in the wrong direction. He leads the league in turnover-worthy play rate and has posted a combined sub-50 passer rating across three consecutive losses.

By no means has Young become a star, but he limits turnovers and has a 114.5 passer rating on deep attempts. The trajectory remains promising for the 25-year-old. He at least has some playoff experience under his belt.

With minimal support in New Orleans, the sophomore starter has actually been strong in clutch situations—posting a 106.5 passer rating in the fourth quarter of one-score games. He's a middle-of-the-pack guy in most other respects, but Shough is quite disciplined considering his limited pro experience.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers — Baker Mayfield: 2/10

A bottom-five quarterback this year in both passer rating and QBR, Mayfield has plenty of experience but is inconsistent and generally unreliable. He ranks 45th among 51 qualifying quarterbacks in EPA per dropback and has the worst bad-throw rate among current starters. Yikes.

We're talking about a rookie Day 2 pick with 18 career pass attempts. It's too early to trust Beck. The Cardinals won't need to until at least next year.

Los Angeles Rams — Matthew Stafford: 9/10

Stafford may be the reigning MVP, but his star receivers did a lot of the heavy lifting in 2025. Now, with injuries decimating the receiving corps, age has seemingly caught up to the 38-year-old Stafford in an interception-plagued season. That being said, in the 2025 playoffs, Stafford led two game-winning drives in the fourth quarter or overtime (bringing his total to five in the postseason since 2021) while posting a 109.3 rating with a one-score margin in the final frame of those victories. He also remains one of the league's best in late, close games.

San Francisco 49ers — Brock Purdy: 10/10

A prime MVP candidate as the league's leader in passer rating and QBR, Purdy has a 106.5 rating in the fourth quarter of one-score playoff games since 2022 and has led four playoff game-winning drives in his first four pro seasons. The 26-year-old looks poised to become a megastar and help San Francisco make a Super Bowl run.

The reigning Super Bowl champion posted a 110.2 passer rating in the fourth quarter of one-score games in Minnesota and Seattle in 2024 and 2025. He obviously needed to be trustworthy on that Super Bowl run. Still, he's having a miserable season. There's growing chatter that the Seahawks could be better off with backup Drew Lock, who has outplayed Darnold in relief.

articles.title: Chiefs' Rashee Rice Says He Caught Late Pass Overturned by Review Late in Loss to Bills
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice has no doubt the officials' decision to overturn his would-be reception on third-and-10 late in the fourth quarter of Thursday's loss to the Buffalo Bills was the wrong call.
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice has no doubt the officials' decision to overturn his would-be reception on third-and-10 late in the fourth quarter of Thursday's loss to the Buffalo Bills was the wrong call.

Speaking to reporters after the Chiefs' 13-10 loss, Rice said in no uncertain terms he caught a pass from Patrick Mahomes that would have given Kansas City a first down with 1:47 remaining in the fourth quarter.

"Yes, I did," Rice said when asked if he caught the ball.

Brittany Mahomes Rips Refs for Late Call

Rice appeared to pin the ball to his shoulder as he fell to the ground for an 11-yard gain, which would have given the Chiefs a first down at their own 20.

The Chiefs had all three timeouts remaining and 1:47 on the clock, giving them plenty of time to drive down the field for a potential game-winning field-goal attempt.

Since there was under two minutes left, the NFL replay officials called to look at the play and determined on replay that Rice did not maintain possession.

Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said the game officials told him the decision to overturn it "came from New York" and from his perspective it was "not clear and obvious" to make that call.

Patrick Mahomes told reporters he was initially told they were reviewing the spot to confirm the first down.

"We were first told that they were reviewing the spot, so I didn't even know that we were reviewing the catch," Mahomes said. "From my angle, when I threw the ball, I thought his hand was under the ball."

The Chiefs defense did force a three-and-out on Buffalo's next possession, but their offense followed with a three-and-out of their own and a punt from their own 11-yard line.

Bills punt returner Greg Dortch returned the punt to the Kansas City 39-yard line with four seconds remaining. Despite inclement weather that caused all sorts of issues for both teams throughout the game, Tyler Bass nailed the 57-yard field goal as time expired to give Buffalo a huge win in the race for the No. 1 seed in the AFC.

The Bills (10-1) maintained their lead as they move closer to securing home-field advantage in the playoffs. The Denver Broncos (8-2) are the only other AFC team with fewer than three losses.

articles.title: Giants' Kayvon Thibodeaux Gives Eagles Sarcastic Praise After Stunning Upset of Cowboys
articles.summary: Even though the Philadelphia Eagles helped the New York Giants' odds of winning the NFC East with their upset win over the Dallas Cowboys on Thanskgiving Day, the rivalry is too strong for Kayvon Thibodeaux to be completely gracious.
articles.body:
Even though the Philadelphia Eagles helped the New York Giants' odds of winning the NFC East with their upset win over the Dallas Cowboys on Thanskgiving Day, the rivalry is too strong for Kayvon Thibodeaux to be completely gracious.

After the Eagles pulled off a stunning 39-38 win over Dallas, Thibodeaux offered a sarcastic thanks to the "pigeons" on X.

The Eagles trailed by 21 points late in the third quarter, then proceeded to outscore Dallas 22-7 in the fourth to steal a win and earn their second consecutive victory following a seven-game losing streak.

It was the largest comeback win for a team on a Thanksgiving day game in NFL history.

Even though Thibodeaux did not really play into the spirit of the Thanksgiving holiday with the tenor of his comment, the Eagles did give New York a lot to be thankful for on Thursday.

Per NFL.com , the Giants' playoff odds are currently at 68 percent. The Cowboys now sit at eight percent to make the postseason.

If the Giants defeat the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday, their odds jump up to 77 percent. Even if they were to lose, they are still better than 50 percent to make the field.

Sometimes, though, the power of the rivalry supersedes everything else. It also helps that the Giants already have a win over the Eagles this season, so Thibodeaux perhaps feels very good about things right now.

It is interesting to note that the Giants and Eagles play again in Week 18. If the Giants don't have a playoff berth secured by that time, the game could end up having huge ramifications.

articles.title: Tom Brady and Terry Bradshaw roast Aaron Rodgers for McCarthy breakup; both feuded with their coaches
articles.summary: Tom Brady and Terry Bradshaw blasted Aaron Rodgers over his Mike McCarthy criticism, but the NFL analysts' own coach feuds tell a similar tale.
articles.body: It was open season on Aaron Rodgers when Super Bowl ring stockpilers Terry Bradshaw and Tom Brady cooked the former Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback from their NFL analyst perches on Thursday. Brady, working the Philadelphia Eagles' shocking comeback win over the Dallas Cowboys for Fox, lectured Rodgers for his handling of the Mike McCarthy claims and how the sanctity of an NFL locker room and appreciating and covering for teammates and coaches is a must. Bradshaw, in studio for Fox, said he was not surprised Rodgers went public with "all his gripes and complaints" because "in my opinion, he's a strange guy, anyway." FORMER STEELERS COACH MIKE TOMLIN CALLS STEELERS SITUATION FOLLOWING AARON RODGERS VS. MIKE MCCARTHY FEUD 'A DUMPSTER FIRE' The former Steelers quarterback, who helped the franchise win four Super Bowls in the 1970s and 1980s, also went on a rant about how athletes should not "turn on our teammates, we don't turn on our coaching staff, we don't turn on our ownership." It was a good basting of Rodgers on Thanksgiving. But it also lacked some important historical context. My take here is not a defense of Aaron Rodgers. But it is a defense of what is true. And while it is true Tom Brady was the most accomplished NFL quarterback of all time and Bradshaw was a Hall of Famer on one of the NFL's greatest dynasties, there is history worth pointing out in this discussion about Rodgers. Both talked extensively about the need to defend teammates while failing to recognize that during his 34-minute appearance on "The Pat McAfee Show" on Wednesday, Rodgers never once criticized a teammate. He aimed his criticism entirely at Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy and the organization's handling of his benching. Rodgers, in fact, explained he confronted McCarthy directly because he understood he was the only player in the locker room with the status to do it, while younger teammates with less job security couldn't, even though he claims they shared his frustration. "I played for my teammates, I played for my coaches," Brady said. "There's nobody that wins when the family feuds." To which he could have been asked if anyone wins when half the family suffers in silence because the guy running it is falling asleep, or ordering ice cream deliveries, or being late, or skipping practices? And, yes, it can be argued Rodgers threw a proverbial stick of dynamite at McCarthy, and his teammates in the locker room had to scurry to snuff it out when reporters asked them questions. AARON RODGERS NOT RETURNING TO STEELERS, SAYS MIKE MCCARTHY FALLS ASLEEP IN MEETINGS AND IS 'UNWELL' But, amazingly, not one current Steelers player said Rodgers was saying things that were untrue despite having that opportunity. And this: At halftime of NBC's Sunday Night Football game, former Steelers coach Mike Tomlin said Rodgers is "beloved" by his teammates. AARON RODGERS AND MIKE MCCARTHY DISAGREEMENTS AT HEART OF QUARTERBACK'S BENCHING BY THE STEELERS "That is real," Tomlin said in a portion of the interview that did not air on NBC. "The guys in that locker room love and appreciate Aaron Rodgers." Both Bradshaw and Brady criticized Rodgers for raising the Steel Curtain of confidentiality and exposing McCarthy's failings. Both thought the Rodgers criticism was untoward. And that's a fair opinion in a vacuum. It is not the same thing, but in 2017 television cameras caught Brady publicly berating Patriots offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels in front of teammates, a full stadium, and the audience at home. And it is indisputable that Brady's relationship with Bill Belichick during their final year was a public soap opera. There were widespread media reports during the 2019 season of tension and a looming split between Brady and Belichick and it reached national news heights. Both denied the reports publicly. So Brady definitely didn't do anything close to what Rodgers just did with his scorched-earth interview. But how do we think the voluminous reports of a rift got out? It was because while Brady wasn't publicly talking about his frustrations, his confidants were. They served as his voice. Also, it happened to a degree in Tampa Bay – again with extensively reported disagreements between Brady and Bruce Arians over offensive philosophy and play-calling. We saw a replay of what happened in New England because, once again, people close to Brady spoke to reporters about the quarterback's frustrations. As for Bradshaw, well, his defense of Steelers ownership and its coach was impressive. But there is some history worth considering. Bradshaw actually stayed away from the Steelers organization for about 20 years because he had a serious dislike for his coach, Chuck Noll, and owner Dan Rooney. Bradshaw didn't think it was good for Rodgers to air dirty laundry about McCarthy publicly, but in the wake of winning four Super Bowl victories, Bradshaw vented to the press about Noll's conservative play-calling and harsh criticism. "We show class on the way out," Bradshaw said on air. "Aaron Rodgers didn't do that." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Bradshaw apparently overlooked that his breakup with Noll was one for the ages, with him telling reporters he was "bitter" that Noll told other reporters the quarterback was "ready for his life's work," meaning his days after football. When Noll died in 2014, Bradshaw skipped his funeral, pointing to his distaste for the coach spanning 40 years. When Rooney died in 2017, Bradshaw skipped his funeral as well, explaining he didn't really know him "that well." But there was Bradshaw on Thursday talking about the Rooneys in glowing terms. None of this context was applied to the analysis of Aaron Rodgers, in which quarterbacks with a history of disagreeing with their coaches, gave Rodgers no grace. It seems, for them, style trumps substance. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

articles.title: Parker Washington Injury Update, Latest on Jaguars WR's Status vs. Titans, Return Timeline
articles.summary: In a surprise turn of events for the Jacksonville Jaguars, Parker Washington will miss at least one game due to a shoulder injury.
articles.body:
In a surprise turn of events for the Jacksonville Jaguars, Parker Washington will miss at least one game due to a shoulder injury.

Head coach Liam Coen announced on Friday that Washington aggravated an AC joint injury in practice and will be out for Sunday's game against the Tennessee Titans.

Coen added Washington is considered week-to-week at this point.

The Jaguars added Washington to their injury report on Thursday. He was a limited participant in practice with a shoulder injury.

This is the first time all season Washington has been listed on the injury report, let alone missing a game. He last sat out a game due to an injury in Week 14 last season against the Indianapolis Colts due to a hip issue.

Depending on the severity of the AC joint injury, recovery times can range from as little as two weeks up to at least 12 weeks. There was no indication from Coen to believe it's a severe injury.

Losing Washington takes a huge piece out of the Jacksonville offense. He leads the team in receptions (44), receiving yards (748) and receiving touchdowns (six). The 24-year-old has posted more than 100 yards in each of the past two games.

Jakobi Meyers and Josh Cameron will likely be the top two receivers for the Jaguars on Sunday. Brian Thomas Jr. figures to see more snaps against the Titans with Washington out of the lineup.

Coen could also design more offensive snaps for Travis Hunter if he wants to get creative in this game. Hunter hasn't played more than nine snaps on offense in a game this season.

The Jaguars are coming off a 23-18 loss to the New York Giants in Week 11. They did defeat the Titans 40-23 when these two teams met at Nissan Stadium on Nov. 15.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes' Wife Brittany Calls Out Refs For Overturned Catch Late in Chiefs' Loss to Bills
articles.summary: If there is a line of Kansas City Chiefs supporters organizing to get off their takes about the controversial Rashee Rice overturned reception against the Buffalo Bills, Brittany Mahomes is probably leading the group.
articles.body:
If there is a line of Kansas City Chiefs supporters organizing to get off their takes about the controversial Rashee Rice overturned reception against the Buffalo Bills, Brittany Mahomes is probably leading the group.

Brittany, Patrick Mahomes' wife, used her Instagram Story after the Chiefs' 13-10 loss on Thursday night to blast the officials for the call late in the fourth quarter.

Brittany Mahomes is not afraid to publicly call out the officials when she thinks the Chiefs are getting squeezed. She did it earlier this month after Kansas City's 28-24 loss to the Denver Broncos when a potential go-ahead touchdown in the final seconds was wiped out because of a false-start penalty against Jaylon Moore.

The sentiment from Mahomes was probably shared among many in the Kansas City area.

Rice appeared to make a clean catch on third-and-10 that would have given the Chiefs a first down with under two minutes remaining in the fourth quarter and the score tied at 10.

The replay official reviewed the play and overturned the call, leading to Kansas City punting. Neither offense could sustain much momentum throughout the game because weather conditions in Buffalo were ugly with a combination of rain and wind.

Even if Rice's play had been ruled a catch, the Chiefs would have had a first down at their own 20-yard line. They only had three drives in the game that gained more than 20 yards, but a first down could have at least forced the Bills to start using their timeouts.

Instead, the Bills were able to save all three timeouts that they would then use on Kansas City's ensuing offensive possession. The strategy worked because Buffalo was able to force a three-and-out, then Greg Dortch returned a punt 17 yards to get the Bills in position to kick the game-winning field goal with four seconds left.

Tyler Bass answered the call with a 57-yard kick that split the uprights to give Buffalo a crucial win in the battle for home-field advantage in the AFC.

The loss dropped Kansas City to 8-3 overall and one game behind the Broncos (8-2) in the loss column for first place in the AFC West.

articles.title: Steelers' Players Reaction to Aaron Rodgers' Exit, Mike McCarthy Remarks Revealed in New NFL Rumors
articles.summary: As the Pittsburgh Steelers look to get back on track and keep their playoff hopes alive amid all the off-field chaos around the organization this week stemming from Aaron Rodgers' comments about Mike McCarthy, players are trying to get ready for their game on Friday against the Denver Broncos.
articles.body:
As the Pittsburgh Steelers look to get back on track and keep their playoff hopes alive amid all the off-field chaos around the organization this week stemming from Aaron Rodgers' comments about Mike McCarthy, players are trying to get ready for their game on Friday against the Denver Broncos.

Appearing on ESPN Radio's Unsportsmanlike , ESPN's Brooke Pryor explained Steelers players are "shellshocked" by everything that has gone down and there is a lot of "confusion and discontent" in the locker room right now.

After the Steelers announced late Tuesday night that Rodgers would be inactive for their game against the Broncos and Mason Rudolph was starting at quarterback, the outspoken quarterback went on The Pat McAfee Show the next day to air out seemingly every grievance he has ever had with McCarthy.

Among the notable comments from Rodgers were saying McCarthy fell asleep in team meetings, breaking down the halftime locker room huddle in a game against the Philadelphia Eagles by saying "1-2-3 Packers" and suggesting there is something wrong with the coach's health.

McCarthy did acknowledge the "1-2-3 Packers" thing was true, calling it an "embarrassing" moment.

Pryor corroborated Rodgers' account with Steelers sources, including one who said "it's all true."

Steelers owner Art Rooney II responded to the situation on Thursday, telling Gerry Dulac of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette that Rodgers' "insubordination will not be tolerated" in the wake of the veteran quarterback being released by the team.

Rooney went on to say he has "100% confidence in Mike McCarthy" and anticipates he will be their head coach "this season, next season and beyond."

As all of this was going on across a 24-hour period between Tuesday and Wednesday, Steelers players also had to practice and prepare for a crucial matchup against the Broncos as they look to remain in control of their playoff destiny.

The Steelers (6-4) have lost two straight games and currently sit in the final wild-card spot in the AFC. Rudolph will be making his first start since Week 12 of the 2025 season. His last win as a starting quarterback came against the New England Patriots in Week 9 of the 2024 campaign.

articles.title: Darian Mensah Falls in Mel Kiper's New 2027 NFL Draft Big Board Rankings, Did Arch Make Top 25?
articles.summary: Miami quarterback Darian Mensah dropped two spots and Texas quarterback Arch Manning didn't make the cut in ESPN NFL draft expert Mel Kiper Jr.'s latest big board for the 2027 NFL draft.
articles.body:
Miami quarterback Darian Mensah dropped two spots and Texas quarterback Arch Manning didn't make the cut in ESPN NFL draft expert Mel Kiper Jr.'s latest big board for the 2027 NFL draft.

Mensah fell from No. 7 to No. 9 in Kiper's rankings, making him the No. 3 quarterback in the draft behind Oklahoma State's Drew Mestemaker and Notre Dame's CJ Carr.

Meanwhile, Manning did not make Kiper's top 25, and he ranked Manning as the No. 7 quarterback behind Mestemaker, Carr, Mensah, Oregon's Dante Moore, Ole Miss' Trinidad Chambliss and South Carolina's LaNorris Sellers.

Mensah has been in the thick of the Heisman Trophy race all season long, leading the Hurricanes to a 10-1 start.

The Duke transfer is completing a remarkable 75.4 percent of his passes for 3,317 yards, 29 touchdowns and four interceptions, while also rushing for 168 yards and two scores.

Although Mensah dipped slightly in Kiper's rankings with Georgia linebacker Chris Cole and LSU offensive tackle Jordan Seaton moving past him, he maintained his spot as Kiper's No. 3 quarterback.

Manning's fall on Kiper's big board has been far more precipitous in recent weeks.

In Kiper's previous rankings , Manning was the No. 25 overall player and No. 6 quarterback, and he was the No. 22 overall player in the rankings before that.

Manning entered the 2026 college football season as a leading Heisman Trophy contender, but he has experienced his fair share of ups and downs.

The nephew of legendary NFL quarterbacks Peyton and Eli Manning has completed 66.2 percent of his passing attempts for 2,485 yards and 21 touchdowns, although his 10 interceptions are cause for concern.

He also hasn't had as much success running the ball as he did last season, going from 399 yards and 10 touchdowns to 170 yards and four scores.

Even so, Manning has led the Longhorns to a 9-2 record and the No. 3 spot in the College Football Playoff rankings.

With a win at Texas A&M on Friday night, Texas would almost certainly clinch a spot in the CFP, and it can secure a spot in the SEC Championship Game with a win and some other results working in its favor.

Performing well in high-stakes games for the remainder of the season could go a long way toward improving Manning's draft stock, but even if he doesn't, it is still easy to envision a team taking a chance on him in the first round of the 2027 NFL draft thanks to his impressive pedigree.

articles.title: Eagles Troll Cowboys With 'National Lampoon' Video After Stunning Upset in Thanksgiving Game
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles added insult to injury after their come-from-behind, 39-38 road victory over the Dallas Cowboys on Thanksgiving.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles added insult to injury after their come-from-behind, 39-38 road victory over the Dallas Cowboys on Thanksgiving.

In a post on X, the Eagles trolled their NFC East rivals by altering a famous clip from the beloved holiday movie National Lampoon's Christmas Vacation:

The scene features Clark Griswold excitedly carving into a turkey, only to be disappointed by how dry it is. However, in the Eagles' version, Griswold was wearing a Cowboys hat, and he was shocked by the final score of Thursday's game.

Philly overcame a 21-point, second-half deficit to improve to 4-7 and remain in the NFC East race thanks to the play of quarterback Joe Milton III, who finished with 331 yards, three touchdowns and one interception through the air, as well as 15 yards and a score on the ground.

articles.title: With Cowboys' season in shambles, how do they avoid a similar fiasco next season?
articles.summary: The Cowboys had a horrendous loss on Thanksgiving to the Eagles.
articles.body:
There have been some horrific Dallas Cowboys losses in their long history.

They lost an NFC championship game on "The Catch," and another when they had a shot at a three-peat. They've lost multiple Super Bowls. There was the playoff game in Seattle when Tony Romo dropped the field goal snap.

So it's hard to say the loss on Thanksgiving this year was the worst the franchise has experienced. But it was bad. Really bad. Leading by 21 points against an Eagles team that lost Saquon Barkley early to injury, was on its third quarterback this season in Joe Milton III and had lost seven of eight, Dallas somehow couldn't close out the win. It was the biggest collapse by any team in a loss in NFL Thanksgiving history.

The worst part is it felt familiar. In Week 8 of this season the Cowboys had a similar failure, losing in overtime to a Cardinals team (now 3-8) after Arizona had benched its quarterback while trailing 24-10 in the fourth quarter.

"Pretty stunning," Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott told the media afterward . "I guess I said it a couple weeks ago after the Arizona game, how stunning that one was, but this definitely takes the cake."

The worst part might be that the Cowboys are again wasting a season of Prescott's prime. He is leading a tremendous offense and if he had more help he'd be getting NFL MVP consideration. But it's looking very unlikely he and the Cowboys will make the playoffs, at a hugely disappointing 5-7.

It seems hopeless going forward. Owner Jerry Jones and his staff need to make sure there's not a repeat in 2027. But how?

The Jerry Jones/Brian Schottenheimer conundrum

The first question that will come up in the offseason, because it has come up after just about every bad loss this season, is if head coach Brian Schottenheimer will be back. He was a surprising hire and is 12-16-1 as Cowboys coach. It's hard to say the Cowboys are playing to their talent level under Schottenheimer.

And yet, Jones has been stubborn about defending Schottenheimer. In one of the more shocking quotes of the season, Jones was asked after the Cardinals debacle about his coach and he absolved his coach from the blame.

"I will say that a lot of people let Brian down today," Jones said after the Cardinals loss, via Associated Press.

Jones' myopia about his head coach is intensely frustrating to Cowboys fans. They see the issues, but Jones continues to blame everything but his head coach. While Jones once again said he wasn't considering staff changes after the Eagles loss, his "question everything" comment might give hope to Cowboys fans who want Schottenheimer gone.

"These are setbacks and they're damning setbacks, there's no question about it," Jones said, according to ESPN . "And especially when we feel like that we can look at parts of the game where it was ours to take and we didn't. So when you look at every bit of it, then you have to question everything."

But Jones has been notoriously and strangely cheap about coaches. He doesn't want to pay buyouts for coaches who have been fired. He said earlier this season on 105.3 The Fan there's "zero correlation" between paying coaches and winning. Maybe the Cowboys will be stuck with a coach who Jones seems intent on keeping so he can learn on the job, when there's no evidence he's getting the most out of his team, or even close.

Most NFL franchises would fire the head coach who has been inadequate so far and the incredibly wealthy owner would pay whatever he has in order to land the best possible candidate to lead his talented team. That's clearly a move that needs to be made for 2027. And maybe Jones will fire Schottenheimer. But it's also fair if Cowboys fans have given up that hope, or don't believe that Jones can identify the right hire or pay a top candidate. At very least Dallas seems like it will make changes among the defensive assistants. But the Cowboys did that last season, and also demoted defensive Christian Parker a couple weeks ago, and nothing has worked.

The lack of urgency from Jones when it comes to his head coach has to be frustrating to the offensive players who are doing their jobs quite well.

Prescott will be 34 years old next season. While that's not ancient for a quarterback, he's running out of time to finally break through to at least an NFC championship game, which hasn't happened yet. And wasting another year of Prescott's prime isn't the only issue.

George Pickens is on the one-year franchise tag and could be gone after this season. CeeDee Lamb is going to be 28. Javonte Williams is 27, but has had a huge workload the past two seasons, an injury history and 27 isn't that young for an NFL running back. The offense might not look the same next season, and if it wasn't for that offense the Cowboys might be the worst team in the NFL.

The defense is horrible. Milton has some great physical tools, but his 331-yard, three-touchdown game on Thursday was unlike any other he had ever had in the NFL. The Cowboys' defense can make anyone look good.

And the simple answer for the offseason is to fix the defense. But that won't be easy. After a trade for cornerback Joey Porter Jr. that hasn't made much impact, the Cowboys have just three picks in the 2027 NFL Draft and six in 2028. Dallas is currently 21st in projected salary-cap space ($16.6 million) via Spotrac , which isn't that bad but they also need to figure out what to do with Pickens and Porter, who will be free agents. If the Cowboys shipped off second- and sixth-round picks to Pittsburgh in a trade for Porter and don't re-sign him, it'll look like another botched move from the front office. If they do re-sign Porter and/or Pickens, there won't be enough cap space to do much else.

And if this all sounds bleak for the Cowboys, it might be. They have an owner who either will keep a coach nobody in Texas wants anymore, or he will not pay up for the best possible coach on the market based on his history. Personnel-wise the Cowboys need to make multiple additions to fix the defense but don't have the cap space or draft picks to do that without getting creative and also hitting home runs on some cheap options. Even the offense isn't guaranteed to look the same with everyone being a year older and Pickens' future very much in the air. Another franchise tag for Pickens would be about $32.8 million .

Perhaps there's a head-coaching change, Jones actually pays up for a top candidate on the market, some of the young defensive players like rookie safety Caleb Downs improve and the offense maintains its level. Then perhaps Dallas gets out of this playoff drought and makes a run. But watching the Cowboys fall apart, yet again, to a beleaguered Eagles team on Thanksgiving, the thought of Dallas being a Super Bowl contender seems far, far off without any great path to a quick fix.

articles.title: Jerry Jones Reveals If He Regrets Waiving Joe Milton III After Eagles' Historic Rally vs. Cowboys
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones was asked if he regretted waiving quarterback Joe Milton III after watching him lead the Philadelphia Eagles to a 39-38 victory over the Cowboys on Thanksgiving Day.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones was asked if he regretted waiving quarterback Joe Milton III after watching him lead the Philadelphia Eagles to a 39-38 victory over the Cowboys on Thanksgiving Day.

"We've seen [Milton] have the kind of plays that he had out there tonight, but that is the best I've seen him play," Jones told reporters after the game. "And he picked a bad time to do it from my standpoint."

Brady Hypes Milton's 'Piss Missile' Throw

The Cowboys entered the fourth quarter with a 31-17 lead before suffering a historic collapse in the fourth quarter. Milton scored on a 15-yard rush and threw a 24-yard touchdown pass to wide receiver Makai Lemon. Philadelphia also scored on a blocked punt that was returned for a touchdown, and kicker Jake Elliott clinched the victory with a 59-yard field goal.

Milton finished with 331 passing yards with three touchdowns and one interception.

Milton was selected by the New England Patriots in the sixth round of the 2024 NFL Draft, but he was traded to Dallas after his rookie season. He served as a backup for Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott in 2025, but Dallas waived him before the start of the 2026 season. The Cowboys were hoping to add Milton to their practice squad after he cleared waivers, per ESPN . Instead, the Eagles swooped in to pick him up.

The Cowboys fell to a 5-7 record and currently rank third in the NFC East.

articles.title: Tom Brady Hyping Joe Milton's 'Piss Missile' Throw Featured in Funny Quote from Eagles vs. Cowboys
articles.summary: Amid the many takeaways from Joe Milton's first career Thanksgiving Day victory in leading the Philadelphia Eagles to a historic comeback over the Dallas Cowboys is he managed to impress arguably the greatest quarterback of all-time.
articles.body:
Amid the many takeaways from Joe Milton's first career Thanksgiving Day victory in leading the Philadelphia Eagles to a historic comeback over the Dallas Cowboys is he managed to impress arguably the greatest quarterback of all-time.

During Fox Sports' broadcast of the game, Tom Brady referred to one of Milton's passes as a "piss missile."

That particular description has become one of Brady's go-to phrases when he is particularly impressed by the arm strength on display by a quarterback. He has even used it for a Dak Prescott throw in Week 2 against the Washington Commanders.

Brady later said he was "kind of embarrassed" about saying it on mic.

"There's a lot of grandmas at home that probably aren't very happy with my mouth on FOX," Brady said. "I'm going to fix that. Sorry, I apologize."

With respect to the grandmas who may have been watching on Thursday, it's hard to argue with Brady's description of Milton's arm strength because it is what stood out most about him as a draft prospect in 2024.

Milton used that arm talent to throw for 331 yards and three touchdowns against the Cowboys. He also ran for a 15-yard touchdown to help the Eagles pull off the largest Thanksgiving Day comeback in NFL history after trailing by as many as 21 points.

articles.title: Cowboys' Brian Schottenheimer Defends Team's Culture After Shocking Loss to Eagles, 'Very Strong'
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer defended his team's culture after their 39-38 loss against the Philadelphia Eagles on Thanksgiving.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer defended his team's culture after their 39-38 loss against the Philadelphia Eagles on Thanksgiving.

"I still believe in our culture," Schottenheimer told reporters Friday. "I think it's very strong. These guys are hurting right now. As they should be. We all are hurting right now. Why? Because we love and care for one another and we want to win."

The Eagles erased a 21-point deficit in the fourth quarter to defeat Dallas, marking the largest Thanksgiving Day comeback in NFL history, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter .

"I think you watch the way our guys played in that game [yesterday], they emptied their tanks," Schottenheimer said. "They played really, really hard. You can't miss watching Quinnen Williams chase and run, and Dak Prescott dive through the air on a big touchdown run and not know that we got the right type of young men. We just got to execute and coach a little bit cleaner and find a way to win games."

Eagles quarterback Joe Milton III, who spent last season with the Cowboys, potentially took a slight jab at the Cowboys during his postgame interview.

"I mean, it was just great coming back here and playing in this stadium in Jerry's World ... but, I mean, it's about the Eagles," Nick Harris of the Fort Worth Star-Telegram. "These guys show up every day. Nobody's late to anything. Nobody's complaining about anything. That's all you can ask for. That's the most important thing that I love about this team. I just know they're going to keep fighting."

Houston Texans tight end Dalton Schultz was also critical of the Cowboys after leaving the team in 2024, comparing the team facility, which provides fans to tours while players are in the building, to a zoo .

The Cowboys entered the 2026 season with high expectations. During the team's training camp, quarterback Dak Prescott nicknamed his offensive unit " GOTI " — an acronym for "Greatest Offense There Is." Despite the offense living to Prescott's hype, the Cowboys immediately struggled, losing four of their first six games to start the season. They still haven't been able to string together back-to-back wins and have fallen to third in the NFC East with a 5-7 record.

Dallas has struggled on defense all season, resulting Mike Pettine replacing defensive coordinator Christian Parker as play-caller ahead of last week's win against the Tennessee Titans.

Cowboys owner Jerry Jones continued to support his head coach when he was asked after the game if Schottenheimer is still the right coach to get the team to the Super Bowl, per The Athletic's Jon Machota .

Dallas will face the Seattle Seahawks on Monday Night Football before heading into their bye in Week 14.

articles.title: Caleb Williams Drops Epic Quote in Video After Clutch TD in Bears' Thanksgiving Win vs. Lions
articles.summary: Caleb Williams acknowledged his "Iceman" alter ego after leading the Chicago Bears to a thrilling comeback victory over the Detroit Lions on Thanksgiving Day.
articles.body:
Caleb Williams acknowledged his "Iceman" alter ego after leading the Chicago Bears to a thrilling comeback victory over the Detroit Lions on Thanksgiving Day.

Following his go-ahead touchdown pass to Rome Odunze in the final seconds, Williams was heard telling his Bears teammates "that's why I'm Ice, baby" as he was dapping them up on the bench.

Williams received the "Iceman" moniker last season for his ability to come up big in clutch situations.

"I'm a fan of it," Williams said about the nickname in November 2025. "It's a cool name. It's interesting when you think of it. Ice is still. Ice is calm, but underneath is pure energy. That's the same mindset I have in those moments. I feel at my calmest on the outside, but there's a lot going on in the inside."

Even though there has been much less need for the late-game dramatics this season because the Bears have largely dominated the opposition, Thursday was a huge moment in the NFC North race.

The Bears (9-2) moved into first place in the division with their 39-35 win over the Lions. They are also one game back in the loss column of the San Francisco 49ers for the No. 1 seed and home-field advantage in the NFC.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers' Mike McCarthy Comments Discussed by NFL Insiders After Steelers Exit, 'Did Him Dirty'
articles.summary: Several NFL insiders defended Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy after quarterback Aaron Rodgers criticized him this week.
articles.body:
Several NFL insiders defended Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy after quarterback Aaron Rodgers criticized him this week.

Rodgers shocked the football world when he appeared Wednesday on the Pat McAfee Show and levied numerous allegations against McCarthy in the wake of the coach benching him in favor of Mason Rudolph:

The veteran signal-caller, who was released shortly after speaking out against McCarthy, accused the head coach of showing up late to meetings, falling asleep during meetings and breaking down the team huddle with "1-2-3, Packers," rather than "1-2-3, Steelers."

The Athletic's Jonathan Jones spoke to many people within the NFL, some of whom have experience working with McCarthy, and the majority of them backed the longtime coach.

An anonymous coach said, "I don't know what [Rodgers] is talking about. Mike is a great coach. The fact he is saying things like that to the media is not coming from a pure heart."

Another coach added, "Mike is one of if not the smartest/best coaches in the business. Genuinely cares about the locker room and everyone around him. I never had any issues with him. Would do anything for him. Every relationship is going to have hard times, especially when you spend as many hours together as you do."

While a league executive acknowledged McCarthy's potential shortcomings, they also called out Rodgers for his handling of the situation, saying, "He got comfortable being a Super Bowl-winning coach and packed it in. Lost his Pittsburgh roots. Just a shame [Rodgers] did him dirty."

Jones reported that he was able to confirm much of what Rodgers about McCarthy said was true, although he also reported that Rodgers essentially tried to stage a "coup" in the form of taking offensive play-calling duties from McCarthy.

Instead, McCarthy benched Rodgers, and the Steelers organization backed McCarthy's decision before ultimately parting ways with the future Hall of Fame quarterback as well.

All of that drama comes amid a 6-4 season for the Steelers, who hold a playoff spot in the AFC entering play on Friday.

An upset win over the Denver Broncos on Friday could go a long way toward strengthening the Steelers' playoff positioning and taking some heat off of McCarthy.

articles.title: Patriots vs. Chargers Friday injury report: Three starters ruled out, Christian Barmore questionable
articles.summary: Game designations for Week 12 at SoFi Stadium.
articles.body:
The New England Patriots will officially be without three against the Los Angeles Chargers.

Quarterback Drake Maye, wide receiver A.J. Brown and cornerback Carlton Davis III have been ruled out ahead of the trip to SoFi Stadium, as head coach Mike Vrabel confirmed during his final press conference of the week. Due to a fractured fibula, a hamstring injury and a knee injury, respectively, each starter remained sidelined throughout preparations following the bye.

Defensive tackle Christian Barmore marked a new absence prior to the flight to California, however, and will be among the questionable.

Here's the early game designations leading up to Sunday's 4:05 p.m. ET kickoff.

The Patriots have utilized seven of eight return designations from injured reserve. And for now, the light will be left on under center for a potential return later in the regular season. Backup Tommy DeVito will get his first start since 2024 on Sunday in the absence New England's 24-year-old captain. Rookie Behren Morton, who has served as the emergency third quarterback, is also in line to be active for the first time in his NFL career.

Out wide, a multiweek hamstring injury sustained during the Munich trip will keep Brown from taking the field at SoFi Stadium. The June trade acquisition's inaugural campaign in Foxborough has brought 11 receptions for 128 yards across 26 targets. A high ankle sprain and knee concerns previously sidelined No. 1. He's made just four starts this fall.

As for Davis, the veteran cornerback has been limited to a handful of appearances after previously working through a neck injury and now working through a knee injury that left him ruled out prior to the bye.

New England returned from Thanksgiving without Barmore on the practice fields due to a knee issue. The defensive tackle, who has fallen out of the starting lineup, stands with 4.5 sacks and a forced fumble while seeing 41.8 percent of the defensive snaps in 2026. He enters the weekend as a questionable call.

Additional calls loom, too. After missing four games due to a hamstring injury, the 5-5 Patriots opened starting left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker's 21-day activation window as work on the 1-9 Chargers began. And 48 hours later, wide receiver Romeo Doubs took part in his first practice since going on injured reserve with a shoulder injury. Both March signings have been listed as limited participants since then while awaiting their returns to the 53-man roster.

"Romeo, I would say we'll see how he comes in tomorrow, but I wouldn't anticipate him being up," Vrabel told reporters, while adding that Vera-Tucker will travel with the team to Los Angeles.

The deadline for gameday transactions is set for Saturday at 4 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers free agency odds: Move over Patriots—a new team has joined the chaos
articles.summary: The Aaron Rodgers era is over with the Pittsburgh Steelers and we broke down the latest odds on his next potential team.
articles.body:
With the dust (mostly) settled following this week's drama surrounding Aaron Rodgers, Mike McCarthy and the Pittsburgh Steelers, one thing we know with certainty is that the veteran quarterback has played his last snap with the franchise. After Rodgers said he was done playing for the team after his benching earlier in the week, the Steelers released him shortly after his wild interview on The Pat McAfee Show .

So, what's next for Rodgers, who was believed to be playing his final NFL season? That's anyone's guess, but after the New England Patriots were the lone team listed with odds to be his next team shortly after his release, we now have one more team that appears to be getting some attention.

We're going to break down the latest teams believed to be at least in consideration to potentially sign Rodgers, as a new franchise has joined the Patriots, per Kalshi .

Odds on Aaron Rodgers' next team if he remains in NFL

Even after trading for quarterback Jacoby Brissett, there's apparently some belief that the Ravens could be a long shot to add Rodgers to the roster. For what it's worth, given that the Ravens lost two quarterbacks to injury—Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley—this could be a precautionary move. Still, it's worth noting that there's at least now a second time on the board.

It's also notable that the Patriots have floated around the 6-8% range after initially being listed at 3%. Drake Maye's injury, question marks at quarterback, and whether backup Tommy DeVito can help keep them in the mix in the AFC have left their outlook at the position for the remainder of 2026 up in the air.

The Patriots remain the most realistic and logical landing spot, but there's also the question of whether Rodgers' decision to go scorched earth on McCarthy was enough to end any chance of an NFL return .

articles.title: Eagles’ Will Shipley compares Nick Sirianni fight to Thanksgiving spat with ‘drunk uncle’
articles.summary: Thanksgiving brought up many joyful moments for the NFL fans as they got to see some interesting action heading into the weekend. The Philadelphia Eagles con...
articles.body:
Thanksgiving brought up many joyful moments for the NFL fans as they got to see some interesting action heading into the weekend. The Philadelphia Eagles continued to keep the fans on their toes and pulled off a dramatic comeback against the Dallas Cowboys on Thursday.

The Eagles overcame a 21-point deficit to win 39-38. But the game also saw a heated sideline exchange between running back Will Shipley and head coach Nick Sirianni . The two were caught arguing late in the first quarter after a failed fourth-down play. Shipley later addressed the incident after the game. However, according to ESPN, he hilariously compared the disagreement to a typical Thanksgiving family argument .

"Emotions were running high. Like on Thanksgiving, all families are arguing about politics and the drunk uncle," Shipley said. "I've got so much love for Coach Nick and him as the leader of this football team."

Shipley declined to reveal what the argument was about but said the two had talked it out. Other players also confirmed that the disagreement was behind them.

"They were loving each other up [in the locker room]," left tackle Jordan Mailata said. "I was like, 'Oh, how come I'm not getting hugged like that?'"

Sirianni also had an animated moment after Jake Elliott's 60-yard game-winning field goal. The coach ran toward a group of Eagles fans to celebrate but was held back by head of security Dom DiSandro as he appeared to react to something from the crowd.

The coach has had several back-and-forths with fans in the past, including during games against the Cleveland Browns in 2024 and the Kansas City Chiefs in 2023. He also shouted a message toward the Indianapolis Colts crowd in 2022 after a win.

"He's a passionate guy, bro. I love that. It's who he is. I always tell him, 'Just be who you are,'" Mailata said. "I saw Nick's passion, I love that s***."

Sirianni said he wants to remain himself while keeping his emotions under control.

articles.title: Cardinals QB Carson Beck will miss second straight game, veteran Josh Johnson will start
articles.summary: (AP) — Arizona Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck will miss a second straight game on Sunday against the Washington Commanders as he continues to recov...
articles.body:
TEMPE, Ariz. (AP) — Arizona Cardinals rookie quarterback Carson Beck will miss a second straight game on Sunday against the Washington Commanders as he continues to recover from back spasms.

First-year coach Mike LaFleur made the announcement on Friday, saying Beck could return for the Dec. 6 game against the Philadelphia Eagles.

Josh Johnson will make his second start for the Cardinals in Beck's place. The 40-year-old journeyman completed 18 of 31 passes for 155 yards and a touchdown in a 34-7 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs last week, performing relatively well considering he had been with the Cardinals less than two weeks.

Arizona has a 3-8 record this season and is trying to snap an 11-game home losing streak on Sunday. Johnson is the Cardinals' fourth starting quarterback this season.

The 24-year-old Beck is a third-round pick out of Miami and the Cardinals were hoping to get a lengthy window to evaluate his potential before deciding on their strategy for the 2027 draft. The back injury has complicated that process, though he could still have five more games on the field if he returns against the Eagles.

articles.title: Chris Shula continues to be at his best when the Rams need him most
articles.summary: Chris Shula was at his best against the Packers on Wednesday night, and he could hold the keys to the Rams' success this season.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams put together a complete performance in their Thanksgiving Eve win over the Green Bay Packers , and while many are applauding Blake Corum and the offense's efforts, the defense was dominant for the fifth straight game by adapting to their opponent and overcoming injuries.

In their last four games, the Rams have held each of their opponents to under 14 points, shutting down whatever is being thrown at them. Even in their 35-21 win over the Las Vegas Raiders , the game that kicked off their winning streak, Las Vegas only scored six points in competitive play, with 15 points coming in garbage time.

Defensive coordinator Chris Shula is once again at his best, showing the league what he can do when given the proper tools to succeed. Shula is entering the most important stretch of his coaching career. Already a head coaching candidate, Shula is set to take on the Kansas City Chiefs, San Francisco 49ers, Dallas Cowboys, Tampa Bay Buccaneers, and the Seattle Seahawks twice to close out the season, teams that pose high-powered, diverse attacks that will test Shula's preparation and tactical skills.

If the Rams wish to make the postseason, they will need Shula and his staff to continue their efforts, putting the players in the right positions to succeed. For the man himself, he's about to become one of the most coveted assistants in football as teams prepare to make changes internally across the NFL.

Once on the brink of their season falling apart, the Rams have rallied with a spirit that has overcome so much this season. That's often been a theme since Shula became defensive coordinator, but now he has the unit to close out games, instead of doing just enough for the offense to win it. With control of the pen, the grandson of the legendary Don Shula will write the future for the Rams' 2026 ambitions.

articles.title: Mike McCarthy contract: What we know about Steelers coach's deal
articles.summary: The signs point toward McCarthy sticking in Pittsburgh
articles.body:
Mike McCarthy has felt the heat since Aaron Rodgers unleashed a barrage of claims regarding the coach's health, honesty and commitment to the Pittsburgh Steelers.

The Steelers benched Rodgers for Mason Rudolph on Tuesday, then released the four-time MVP after his comments the following afternoon. Former Pittsburgh coach Mike Tomlin described the situation as a "dumpster fire" during Sunday Night Football .

Team owner Art Rooney II said he has "100% confidence" in McCarthy, and the Steelers are historically patient with their coaches. Still, the spotlight on McCarthy will only grow brighter with the Denver Broncos and their vaunted defense coming to town on Black Friday.

Here's what we know about McCarthy's contract, in the event the Steelers ever consider moving on.

McCarthy signed a five-year deal with the Steelers in January. Financial terms were not disclosed. Since it's his first year, it's highly unlikely McCarthy goes anywhere, at least anytime soon. The Steelers have only four head coaches in the modern era, so it'd be extremely out of character for them to cut bait on McCarthy now, even after a catastrophic week online.

The Browns are getting ready for a primetime matchup with the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday. That doesn't mean there isn't time for a joke or two along the way, especially if you are Grant Delpit.

Rodgers accused their head coach broke down the huddle with a "1, 2, 3, Packers"

articles.title: David Pastrnak Injury Update: Bruins Captain Exits Game vs. Maple Leafs After Non-Contact Injury
articles.summary: David Pastrnak looked to score for the Bruins against the Maple Leafs, but he suffered an injury during the game.
articles.body:
When the Bruins needed all hands on deck, the team took a big hit when captain David Pastrnak was forced to leave a game against the Maple Leafs.

Pastrnak, with one shot attempt on Black Friday, left the game in the first period following a non-contact injury. When he left, the score was 1-1.

The Bruins later deemed him UNLIKELY to play for the rest of the game due to a lower-body injury.

Picked 25th in the 2014 NHL Draft, Pastrnak scored 10 goals in his rookie season. He scored a career-high 61 during the 2022-23 season. Last year, Pastrnak earned 100 points for the fourth straight season. He was named the 28th Bruins captain this year.

Before the injury, Pastrnak led the team with 11 goals, 21 assists, and 32 points.

It's unknown what Pastrnak's status will be for the rest of the game or the Bruins' next game on Sunday against the Canucks.

NESN will provide updates when available.
